definition_zh: 机构的；制度的；体制化的；机构投资者的；机构照护的
definition_en: relating to an institution (an established organization, custom, or system); typical of large organizations; also used in fixed phrases such as institutional investor or institutional care
core_image: 一栋挂着门牌、贴满规章、编好序列号的大楼：人一进门，就被同一套流程接住
scene: 这里指「机构的」。 The reform was blocked less by law than by institutional inertia inside the ministry.
sceneCN: 这里 institutional 是「机构化的、大型机构特有的」（第 3 个义项：按规章办事而缺乏人情味的作风）；句意：改革与其说被法律挡住，不如说被部委内部那种机构惰性挡住。图中可辨识物件：部委走廊、成堆文件、停滞的印章。

pos.zh: 机构的；制度的；体制化的；机构投资者的

derivatives.zh: 使制度化；把某人送入机构
制度主义；对机构的依赖

senses.title: Relating to an established organization
senses.definition: connected with an institution such as a university, bank, hospital, or government body
senses.definitionCN: 与大学、银行、医院或政府机关等机构相关的
senses.example: The report examines the institutional structure of the university.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告考察这所大学的机构结构。
senses.why: Latin instituere means 'to set in place'. An institution is something set up and left standing; institutional describes whatever belongs to that set-up organization.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 instituere 意为「安置、设立」。institution 是被设立并持续站立的东西；institutional 描述属于这一已设立组织的事物。

senses.title: Relating to an established custom or system
senses.definition: connected with a long-established custom, rule, or social system rather than with a single organization
senses.definitionCN: 与长期确立的习俗、规则或社会制度相关，而非与单一组织相关
senses.example: Institutional resistance to change can outlast any single government.
senses.exampleCN: 制度层面对变革的抵制可能比任何一届政府都更持久。
senses.why: The noun institution also names a custom or system that society sets up and keeps standing; the adjective simply extends to that abstract level.
senses.whyCN: 名词 institution 也指社会设立并维持的习俗或制度；形容词只是把意义扩展到这一抽象层面。

senses.title: Typical of a large organization
senses.titleCN: 机构化的；大型机构特有的（常含贬义）
senses.definition: showing the impersonal, rule-bound habits typical of large organizations
senses.definitionCN: 表现出大型组织特有的、按规章办事而缺乏人情味的作风
senses.example: His institutional tone made the apology sound like an internal circular.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套机构化的腔调让道歉听起来像一份内部通函。
senses.why: When an organization grows, its procedures harden; the adjective then describes behaviour shaped by the machinery of the place rather than by a person.
senses.whyCN: 组织变大后，其程序会硬化；这个形容词于是描述由该处机器般流程而非个人塑造的行为。

senses.title: Of an institutional investor
senses.definition: relating to a large organization that invests funds on behalf of others, such as a pension fund or an insurance company
senses.definitionCN: 与代表他人投资的大型组织（如养老基金或保险公司）相关的
senses.example: Institutional buying pushed the share price up sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 机构买盘把股价迅速推高。
senses.why: Finance narrows the word to organizations that invest professionally; the actor is the institution, not a private person.
senses.whyCN: 金融领域把该词窄化为专业投资的机构；行动者是机构，而非私人。

senses.title: Provided by an institution rather than a family
senses.titleCN: 机构照护的；由机构提供的
senses.definition: describing care given in a residential institution rather than at home
senses.definitionCN: 描述在住宿制机构而非在家中提供的照护
senses.example: Demand for institutional care rose as families grew smaller.
senses.exampleCN: 随着家庭规模变小，对机构照护的需求上升。
senses.why: The word marks the provider: care is supplied by an institution, a place set up for that purpose.
senses.whyCN: 该词标明提供者：照护由机构提供，而机构正是为该目的设立的地方。

senses.title: Fixed by convention; routinized
senses.definition: established as a routine or convention, so that it is no longer questioned
senses.definitionCN: 已作为例行程序或惯例确立，因此不再受到质疑
senses.example: The Friday meeting had become an institutional habit no one dared cancel.
senses.exampleCN: 周五的会议已变成一种没人敢取消的机构惯例。
senses.why: What has been set up long enough becomes part of the furniture; institutional here means built into the routine.
senses.whyCN: 被设立得足够久的东西会成为固定陈设；此处 institutional 意为已嵌入例行程序。

senses.title: Relating to institutional advertising
senses.definition: relating to advertising that promotes the image of a company or organization rather than a particular product
senses.definitionCN: 与推广公司或组织形象而非特定产品的广告相关的
senses.example: The firm spent more on institutional advertising than on product campaigns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在机构形象广告上的投入超过产品推广。
senses.why: Such advertising sells the institution itself, its reputation and standing, not a single product on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 这类广告卖的是机构本身，即其声誉与地位，而非货架上的单一产品。

senses.title: Of an ethics or review board
senses.definition: relating to a formal committee that reviews research or ethics within an institution
senses.definitionCN: 与机构内部审查研究或伦理的正式委员会相关的
senses.example: All proposals must pass institutional review before data collection begins.
senses.exampleCN: 所有提案在开始收集数据前都必须通过机构审查。
senses.why: The board acts as the institution in miniature; its authority comes from the organization that sets it up.
senses.whyCN: 该委员会是机构权力的缩影；其权限来自设立它的组织。

senses.title: Built into social structures
senses.titleCN: 制度性的；结构性根源的
senses.definition: describing disadvantages or advantages embedded in the normal workings of social systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述嵌入社会系统正常运作中的劣势或优势
senses.example: The study traces health gaps to institutional factors rather than individual choices.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把健康差距追溯到制度性因素，而非个人选择。
senses.why: Here the institution is not one building but the whole set of standing arrangements; what such arrangements produce is called institutional.
senses.whyCN: 此处的 institution 不是一栋建筑，而是整套长期维持的安排；由这些安排产生的东西便被称为 institutional。

intro.en: Institutional is the adjective of institution with the suffix -al. The chain runs from a reconstructed Indo-European root for 'stand' through Latin stare and statuere to instituere 'set in place', then to Latin institutio, French, and English institution.
intro.cn: institutional 是 institution 加后缀 -al 构成的形容词。链条从表示「站立」的原始印欧语重构词根，经拉丁 stare 与 statuere，到 instituere「安置、设立」，再到拉丁 institutio、法语和英语 institution。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sta- 'to stand' is generally thought to underlie Latin stare. The star marks a reconstructed form, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 原始印欧语重构形式 *sta- 意为「站立」，一般认为它是拉丁 stare 的来源；星号表示重构，并非实际记录的词。

items.en: stare meant 'to stand, be standing'. It is the simple verb of standing that all the stat- words grow from.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、站着」。它是所有 stat- 词族所生长的最简动词。

items.en: statuere is the causative of stare: 'to cause to stand, set up, place'. What is set up is made to stand.
items.cn: statuere 是 stare 的使动形式：「使站立、设立、放置」。被设立的东西就是被使其站立。

items.en: in- 'into, upon' + statuere gives instituere 'to set in place, establish, arrange'. Here in- means 'into or upon', not the negative 'not'.
items.cn: in-「进入、在上」+ statuere 构成 instituere「安置、设立、安排」。这里的 in- 表示「进入、在上」，不是否定前缀「不」。

items.en: institutio meant 'an arrangement, establishment, instruction'. It named both the act of setting up and the thing set up.
items.cn: institutio 意为「安排、设立、教导」。它既指设立的动作，也指被设立的东西。

items.en: Old French passed institution to English in the 14th century. English later added -al to form the adjective institutional, meaning 'of an institution'.
items.cn: 古法语把 institution 传入英语，时为 14 世纪。英语后来加上 -al 构成形容词 institutional，意为「属于机构的」。

note.en: The first group contains near-identical forms whose Latin prefixes or roots differ; the second contains words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形式相近但拉丁前缀或词根不同的词；第二组是意义相近的词。

entries.definition: an established organization or custom; the noun behind institutional
entries.definitionCN: 已建立的组织或习俗；institutional 所源自的名词

entries.definition: relating to a constitution; from con- 'together' + statuere, not in- 'into', and about founding law rather than an organization
entries.definitionCN: 与宪法相关的；来自 con-「一起」+ statuere，而非 in-「进入」，讲的是立国法律而非组织

entries.definition: a learned society or research body; from the same instituere, but the noun usually names one specific body, not a custom
entries.definitionCN: 学会或研究机构；来自同一 instituere，但名词通常指某个特定团体，而非习俗

entries.definition: relating to teaching; from struere 'build', not from stare 'stand', so the shared -ctional shape is misleading
entries.definitionCN: 与教学相关的；来自 struere「建造」，而非 stare「站立」，因此相似的 -ctional 外形具有误导性

entries.definition: relating to the structure of an organization; narrower than institutional, which also covers customs and systems
entries.definitionCN: 与组织结构相关的；比 institutional 窄，后者还涵盖习俗与制度

entries.definition: affecting the whole system; close to sense 09 but stresses the system rather than the established institution
entries.definitionCN: 影响整个系统的；接近第 9 个义项，但强调系统而非已确立的制度

entries.definition: following long-accepted practice; close to sense 06 but without the bureaucratic flavour
entries.definitionCN: 遵循长期接受的做法的；接近第 6 个义项，但没有官僚色彩

entries.definition: run by officials and rules; close to sense 03 but names the administrative machine directly
entries.definitionCN: 由官员和规章运转的；接近第 3 个义项，但直接点明行政机器

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: in- 'into, upon' + statuere 'set, stand' -> set into place -> institutional: of an institution. The in- is not the negative 'not'.
normal.cn: in-「进入、在上」+ statuere「设立、站立」→ 设立进去 → institutional 机构的、制度的。这里的 in- 不是否定「不」。

normal.en: institution is the noun, -al makes the adjective, parallel to constitution and constitutional but with a different prefix.
normal.cn: institution 是名词，-al 构成形容词，与 constitution 和 constitutional 结构平行，但前缀不同。

normal.en: institute is one learned body; institution is the standing arrangement; institutional belongs to the latter and to the wider system.
normal.cn: institute 是某一个学会；institution 是长期维持的安排；institutional 属于后者以及更广的制度。

normal.en: institutionalize = make into an institution; -ize adds 'make', so the suffix marks a change of state.
normal.cn: institutionalize = 使成为制度；-ize 表示「使成为」，标记状态变化。

normal.en: institutional memory means an organization remembers through files, habits, and old staff, not through one mind.
normal.cn: institutional memory 指组织通过档案、习惯和老员工记忆，而不是靠某一个头脑。

abstract.en: Think of a building with a filing system: the building is the institution, and the air inside that shapes everyone is institutional.
abstract.cn: 把机构想象成一栋带档案系统的楼：楼是 institution，楼内塑造每个人的空气是 institutional。

abstract.en: Think of a river bed and its water: the institution is the channel, institutional is the direction the water is forced to take.
abstract.cn: 把制度想象成河床与水：institution 是河道，institutional 是水被迫流去的方向。

abstract.en: Think of a uniform issued by the place: institutional behaviour is the uniform speaking instead of the person.
abstract.cn: 把机构想象成发放制服的地方：机构化行为就是制服在说话，而不是人在说话。

examples.en: Institutional rules slowed the hiring process to a crawl.
examples.cn: 机构规章把招聘流程拖得极慢。

examples.en: The foundation is an institutional investor with a very long horizon.
examples.cn: 该基金会是一家投资期限很长的机构投资者。

examples.en: Researchers submitted the plan to the institutional review board.
examples.cn: 研究人员把方案提交给机构审查委员会。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: in-（向内）+ stituere（设立）：把规矩设立到组织内部 → institutional 机构的、制度的；注意 in- 在此不是「不」

root: 拉丁 instituere「安置、设立」（in-「进入、在上」+ statuere「使站立」，statuere 出自 stare「站立」）；与 constitutional、statute、statue 同出原始印欧语重构词根 *sta-；此处 in- 不是否定前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: something set up and left standing. An organization, a custom, a routine, a review board, and a social structure are all things that stand because they were instituted.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个画面辐射开来：被设立并持续站立的东西。组织、习俗、例行程序、审查委员会和社会结构，都是因为被设立才得以站立。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a set-up structure that stands and shapes whatever passes through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个被设立起来、持续站立并塑造经过其内部一切的结构。

branches.en: ORGANIZATION: the institution as a body, including the board that acts in its name.
branches.cn: 组织：作为团体的机构，包括以其名义行事的委员会。

branches.en: STANDING ARRANGEMENT: customs and routines that stay in place until they feel natural.
branches.cn: 长期安排：习俗与例行程序长期在位，直到显得理所当然。

branches.en: ORGANIZATIONAL MACHINE: the impersonal tone and the image advertising of a large body.
branches.cn: 组织机器：大型机构的非人格化腔调与形象广告。

branches.en: FINANCIAL ACTOR: an institution that invests on behalf of others.
branches.cn: 金融行动者：代表他人投资的机构。

branches.en: EMBEDDED CARE AND STRUCTURE: care provided by a body, and advantages built into society.
branches.cn: 嵌入的照护与结构：由机构提供的照护，以及嵌入社会的优势或劣势。

intro.en: Institutional is institution plus the productive adjective suffix -al, from Latin -alis. The inner in- and statuere are fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: institutional 是 institution 加能产的形容词后缀 -al（来自拉丁 -alis）。内部的 in- 与 statuere 已凝固在词基中。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare 'to stand' and statuere 'set up' produced state, status, statue, statute, institute, institution, constitution, and constant. The reconstructed Indo-European root *sta- is a scholarly reconstruction, not an attested word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare「站立」与 statuere「设立」产生了 state、status、statue、statute、institute、institution、constitution、constant。原始印欧语重构词根 *sta- 是学术重构，并非有记录的实际词。

items.meaning: an established organization or custom; -tion marks the result of setting up
items.meaningCN: 机构；制度（in-「进入」+ statuere + -tion，-tion 标记设立的结果）
items.example: The university is an old institution.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学是一座古老的机构。

items.meaning: of or belonging to an institution
items.meaningCN: 机构的；制度的（institution + -al 形容词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 机构规章管理这一流程。

items.meaning: to set up; as a noun, a learned society or research body
items.meaningCN: 设立；学会或研究机构（由动作名词转为特定团体）
items.exampleCN: 该研究所资助基础研究。

items.meaning: to make something into an institution, or to place someone in one
items.meaningCN: 使制度化；把某人送入机构（-ize 表示「使成为」）
items.example: The practice was institutionalized in the 1950s.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法在 20 世纪 50 年代被制度化。

items.meaningCN: 制度化；机构化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Critics warned against the institutionalization of care.
items.exampleCN: 批评者警告照护过度机构化的风险。

items.meaning: the founding law that sets up a state; con- means together, unlike the in- of institution
items.meaningCN: 宪法（con-「一起」+ statuere + -tion；con- 表示「一起」，不同于 institution 的 in-）
items.example: The constitution sets out basic rights.

items.meaning: a law set in place by authority
items.meaningCN: 法规；成文法（被权威设立之物）
items.example: The statute was passed last year.

items.meaning: a figure set up in a place
items.meaningCN: 雕像（被设立在某处的人像）
items.example: A statue stands in the square.

items.meaning: teaching or an order; root struere means build, not stand
items.meaningCN: 教导；指令（词根 struere 意为建造，而非站立）

latinEntries.meaning: to set in place, establish, arrange

definition_zh: 重婚者；犯重婚罪的人
definition_en: a person who marries another while still legally married to someone else
core_image: 同一人揣着两本结婚证，两场婚礼隔着城市
scene: 两份婚姻档案送进法庭，法官皱起了眉。 The bigamist was arrested soon after the second wedding.
sceneCN: 这里 bigamist 是「重婚者」（第 1 个义项：在婚期间又与他人结婚之人）；句意是重婚者在第二场婚礼后不久被捕。

pos.zh: 重婚者

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「重婚（罪）」，bigamist 由其派生
bigamy 加形容词后缀，义为「重婚的」
同族反义概念，义为「一夫一妻制」

senses.title: One married to two spouses at once
senses.definition: someone who enters a second marriage while the first remains legally valid
senses.definitionCN: 在第一段婚姻仍具法律效力时再缔结婚姻之人
senses.example: The bigamist was arrested soon after the second wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 重婚者在第二场婚礼后不久被捕。
senses.why: Greek bi- means twice and gamos means marriage, so the person has married twice.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 bi- 意为「两次」，gamos 意为「婚姻」，故指结了两次婚的人。

senses.title: One who deceives both spouses
senses.definition: someone concealing an existing marriage from a new partner
senses.definitionCN: 向新伴侣隐瞒已有婚姻之人
senses.example: The bigamist kept two households in different cities.
senses.exampleCN: 重婚者在两个城市各养一个家。
senses.why: Bigamy requires deception, and the deceiver is the bigamist.
senses.whyCN: 重婚必涉欺瞒，行欺瞒者即重婚者。

senses.title: One prosecuted under bigamy law
senses.definition: a defendant charged with the crime of bigamy
senses.definitionCN: 被控重婚罪的被告
senses.example: The court convicted the bigamist of fraud as well.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭同时判该重婚者欺诈罪成立。
senses.why: Naming the person follows the name of the crime.
senses.whyCN: 罪名既立，犯者随之得名。

senses.title: One whose second marriage is void
senses.definition: someone whose later marriage is legally invalid because of the first
senses.definitionCN: 因已有婚姻而使其后缔结的婚姻无效之人
senses.example: As a bigamist, his second ceremony carried no legal weight.
senses.exampleCN: 身为重婚者，他的第二场婚礼毫无法律效力。
senses.why: Law voids the overlap, branding its maker a bigamist.
senses.whyCN: 法律宣告重叠婚姻无效，其缔造者遂成重婚者。

senses.title: Serial or accidental bigamist
senses.titleCN: 惯犯或无心之失的重婚者
senses.definition: a person who commits bigamy repeatedly or through forgotten earlier marriages
senses.definitionCN: 屡次重婚，或因遗忘旧婚而再婚之人
senses.example: The wanderer became a bigamist without remembering his desert marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 流浪者忘了荒漠里那场婚，成了无心重婚者。
senses.why: Intent matters less than the legal fact of two marriages.
senses.whyCN: 比起意图，两段婚姻的法律事实更为关键。

senses.title: In literature, the deceiver figure
senses.definition: a stock character of fiction who keeps parallel married lives
senses.definitionCN: 小说中维持双重婚姻生活的定型人物
senses.example: The novel's bigamist falls when the two letters cross.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里的重婚者因两封信交错寄达而败露。
senses.why: Double lives make the bigamist a dramatic engine.
senses.whyCN: 双重生活使重婚者成为戏剧引擎。

senses.title: Compared with polygamist
senses.definition: one with two overlapping marriages, as distinct from one with many sanctioned spouses
senses.definitionCN: 重叠两次婚姻者，区别于获准多配偶者
senses.example: Unlike a polygamist in a permitted system, the bigamist breaks the law.
senses.exampleCN: 与允许多配偶制度下的多配偶者不同，重婚者触犯法律。
senses.why: Two hidden marriages differ from many open ones.
senses.whyCN: 隐秘的两次婚姻，不同于公开的多偶。

senses.title: One whose bigamy dissolves status
senses.definition: a spouse whose offense ends recognized marital standing
senses.definitionCN: 因重婚罪而失去认可婚姻地位者
senses.example: The bigamist lost custody in the divorce that followed.
senses.exampleCN: 重婚者在随后的离婚官司中失去监护权。
senses.why: The crime dissolves the very status it pretended to keep.
senses.whyCN: 罪行摧毁了它所伪装维系的身份。

intro.en: Bigamist is bigamy, twice-married, plus the agent suffix.
intro.cn: bigamist 由 bigamy「重婚」加施动者后缀构成。

items.en: dwo- meant two; reconstructed form.
items.cn: dwo- 意为「二」（重构形式）。

items.en: bi- (from Latin) plus gamos, marriage, gave digamos, twice married.
items.cn: bi-（经拉丁语）加希腊语 gamos「婚姻」，得 digamos「结过两次婚的」。

items.en: bigamus meant twice married; bigamia, the condition.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bigamus 意为「再婚者」；bigamia 指再婚状态。

items.en: in canon law bigamia narrowed to unlawful second marriage.
items.cn: 在教会法中 bigamia 收窄为非法的第二次婚姻。

items.en: English bigamy took the criminal sense; bigamist names the offender.
items.cn: 英语 bigamy 确立刑事义；bigamist 指犯罪者。

items.en: now a legal and everyday label for one married twice at once.
items.cn: 如今是法律与日常对同时两婚者的称谓。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gam- marriage root; the near-meaning group gathers marriage-law terms.
note.cn: 形近组共享 gam-「婚姻」词根；近义组汇集婚姻法律类词。

entries.definition: the crime of marrying while already married
entries.definitionCN: 重婚罪——bigamist 的基础词

entries.definition: of or guilty of bigamy
entries.definitionCN: 重婚的——形容词形式

entries.definition: one who has several spouses
entries.definitionCN: 多配偶者——同根 poly-（多）

entries.definition: one who is unfaithful to a spouse
entries.definitionCN: 通奸者——不涉及再婚

entries.definition: an intolerant person
entries.definitionCN: 偏执者——拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: one married to a single spouse
entries.definitionCN: 一夫一妻者——同根 mono-（单一）

normalIntro.en: Bigamist is bi- (two) plus gamos (marriage) plus -ist.
normalIntro.cn: bigamist 是 bi-（二）加 gamos（婚姻）加 -ist（人）。

normal.en: Bigamy is the crime; bigamist is the person.
normal.cn: bigamy 是罪名，bigamist 是犯者。

normal.en: The second marriage is void.
normal.cn: 第二次婚姻在法律上无效。

normal.en: Polygamist holds several, not just two.
normal.cn: polygamist 配偶不止两位。

normal.en: Bigamous is the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词是 bigamous。

normal.en: Gamos also gives monogamy and polygamy.
normal.cn: gamos 还构成 monogamy 与 polygamy。

abstract.en: See two wedding rings on one hand.
abstract.cn: 看一只手上戴两枚婚戒。

abstract.en: Feel the double life collapsing at one knock on the door.
abstract.cn: 感受一声敲门让双重生活崩塌。

abstract.en: Picture two wedding albums on the same shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象同一书架上并排的两本婚礼相册。

examples.en: The bigamist was arrested soon after the second wedding.
examples.cn: 重婚者在第二场婚礼后不久被捕。

examples.en: The bigamist kept two households in different cities.
examples.cn: 重婚者在两个城市各养一个家。

examples.en: The court convicted the bigamist of fraud as well.
examples.cn: 法庭同时判该重婚者欺诈罪成立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必·盖」——婚事必有一层盖一层，两本红本子叠着藏，是为重婚。

root: 拉丁语 bi-「二」加希腊语 gamos「婚姻」经拉丁语 bigamus「再婚者」复合；教会法将 bigamia 收窄为非法再婚，英语承其刑事义，bigamist 以施动者后缀 -ist 指称犯者。

sensesIntro.en: From twice-married grows the deceiver, the defendant, the void bridegroom, and the fictional double-lifer.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「两度结婚」长出欺瞒者、被告、二婚无效者与文学中的双重生活者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings, one finger, two lives
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚手指两枚戒，一体两命

branches.en: The overlapping marriages and their nullity
branches.cn: 重叠婚姻及其无效

branches.en: Deception in life and fiction
branches.cn: 现实与文学中的欺瞒

branches.en: Prosecution and loss of status
branches.cn: 被诉与失位

branches.en: Intent and the repeat offender
branches.cn: 意图与惯犯

branches.en: Contrast with sanctioned plural marriage
branches.cn: 与合法多偶的对照

intro.en: Bigamist stacks a number prefix, a Greek marriage root, and an agent suffix.
intro.cn: bigamist 由数词前缀、希腊婚姻词根与施动者后缀叠成。

latinIntro.en: The gamos family through Greek and Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 gamos 词族及其拉丁与英语后裔。

definition_zh: n. 猿；类人猿（无尾）；笨拙的模仿者　v. 模仿；照搬（常含贬义）
definition_en: A large tailless primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee; as a verb, to copy someone's behaviour or style closely and rather clumsily, usually with a hint of criticism.
core_image: 没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍
scene: 小猩猩照着饲养员的动作把毛巾搭在肩上。 The young chimp likes to ape the keeper's gestures.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：动词 ape 指照着别人的样子笨拙模仿，多半带一点贬义。

pos.zh: 猿；类人猿；笨拙的模仿者
模仿；照搬

derivatives.zh: 像猿一样地；笨拙模仿地

senses.title: A tailless primate
senses.definition: a large primate without a tail, such as a gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan or gibbon
senses.definitionCN: 没有尾巴的大型灵长类动物，如大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩或长臂猿
senses.example: The great apes share most of their DNA with humans.
senses.exampleCN: 类人猿与人类共享大部分 DNA。
senses.why: The key contrast with a monkey is the tail: apes have none, and that single feature is what the noun picks out.
senses.whyCN: 与 monkey 的关键区别在尾巴：猿没有尾巴，这个名词抓住的正是这一条特征。

senses.title: To copy clumsily
senses.definition: to imitate someone's actions, voice or style closely, often without understanding, and usually with a disapproving tone
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧照着他人的动作、声音或风格去模仿，往往并不理解，语气多含贬义
senses.example: The band spent a year aping their heroes before finding a voice.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队照搬偶像整整一年，才找到自己的声音。
senses.why: Apes were long thought to mimic human gestures, so the animal name turned into a verb for shallow copying.
senses.whyCN: 人们长期认为猿会模仿人的动作，于是这个动物名变成了表示浅层照搬的动词。

senses.title: A crude imitator
senses.definition: a person who copies others without originality, or who behaves in a rough, foolish way
senses.definitionCN: 毫无原创性地照搬他人的人，或举止粗鲁愚笨的人
senses.example: He was dismissed as an ape of better painters.
senses.exampleCN: 他被看作只会照搬更优秀画家的人而不受重视。
senses.why: This sense keeps both halves of the word at once: the animal and the copying, aimed at a person as an insult.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项同时保留了词的两半：动物与模仿，用作针对人的贬称。

intro.en: Ape is a native Germanic word, Old English apa, related to Dutch aap and German Affe. The verb sense grew out of the belief that apes mimic people.
intro.cn: ape 是日耳曼本族词，古英语作 apa，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源。动词义来自「猿会模仿人」这一观念。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root is apan-, a word for the large tailless primates known in northern Europe.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根是 apan-，指北欧人所知的大型无尾灵长类动物。

items.en: Old English wrote apa for both the animal and, loosely, a fool. The plural was apan.
items.cn: 古英语用 apa 指这种动物，也宽泛地指愚人，复数作 apan。

items.en: Middle English ape kept the animal sense and added the figurative use for someone who copies others.
items.cn: 中古英语 ape 保留动物义，并增加了「照搬他人者」的比喻用法。

items.en: Dutch aap and German Affe are the same word, which shows the term is Germanic rather than borrowed from Latin.
items.cn: 荷兰语 aap 与德语 Affe 是同一个词，说明它是日耳曼词，而非从拉丁语借来。

items.en: Around the 1630s the noun became a verb meaning to mimic, from the popular idea that apes imitate human gestures.
items.cn: 1630 年代前后，名词转动词，意为「模仿」，源自「猿会学人的动作」这一流行观念。

items.en: Modern biology keeps ape for the tailless group, separating it sharply from monkey, which normally has a tail.
items.cn: 现代生物学把 ape 留给无尾类群，与通常有尾的 monkey 明确区分。

note.en: The look-alike group guards against apt and ace, which are only a letter away; the near-meaning group lists verbs for copying.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 apt、ace 混淆；近义组列出表示「模仿」的动词。

entries.definition: Suitable, or quick to learn.
entries.definitionCN: 恰当的；学得很快的。

entries.definition: A top player, or the highest card.
entries.definitionCN: 高手；最大的那张牌。

entries.definition: A sleeveless cloak, or a headland.
entries.definitionCN: 无袖斗篷；海角。

entries.definition: Foolishly imitative.
entries.definitionCN: 傻乎乎地模仿的。

entries.definition: To copy a voice or manner closely.
entries.definitionCN: 逼真地模仿声音或举止。

entries.definition: To do the same as someone else.
entries.definitionCN: 照着别人的样子做。

entries.definition: To copy in order to match or beat.
entries.definitionCN: 为赶上或超越而效法。

entries.definition: To repeat words without thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 不动脑子地重复别人的话。

normalIntro.en: Ape has three letters and no tail: apes are the primates that lost the tail, monkeys kept it.
normalIntro.cn: ape 只有三个字母，也没有尾巴：猿是没尾巴的那一类，猴子留着尾巴。

normal.en: Great apes are gorillas, chimps, orangutans and gibbons.
normal.cn: 类人猿包括大猩猩、黑猩猩、红毛猩猩与长臂猿。

normal.en: The verb is disapproving: aping is copying without thought.
normal.cn: 动词含贬义：aping 是不动脑地照搬。

normal.en: Inflections are apes, aped, aping, with no doubled letter.
normal.cn: 变化形式是 apes、aped、aping，不双写字母。

normal.en: Do not confuse ape with apt, which means suitable.
normal.cn: 别把 ape 与 apt「恰当的」混淆。

normal.en: The adjective apish describes foolish imitation.
normal.cn: 形容词 apish 形容愚蠢的模仿。

abstract.en: Picture a chimp copying a keeper's wave.
abstract.cn: 想象黑猩猩学饲养员挥手。

abstract.en: Imagine a band sounding exactly like its heroes.
abstract.cn: 想象一支乐队听起来和偶像一模一样。

abstract.en: Think of a mirror that only repeats, never adds.
abstract.cn: 想象一面只会重复、从不添东西的镜子。

examples.en: Gibbons are the smallest of the apes.
examples.cn: 长臂猿是猿类中体型最小的。

examples.en: He aped his teacher's accent for a laugh.
examples.cn: 他学老师的口音逗大家笑。

examples.en: The film is aping a style it never understands.
examples.cn: 这部电影照搬了一种它并不理解的风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ape 三个字母，尾巴也「没有」——无尾的是 ape，有尾的是 monkey；动词就是照搬别人的动作。

root: 日耳曼本族词，古英语 apa「猿」，与荷兰语 aap、德语 Affe 同源；因古人认为猿善学人动作，1630 年代生出动词「模仿、照搬」，再引申指拙劣的模仿者。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses run from the animal to the copying: a tailless primate, the act of copying like one, and a person who only copies.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从动物走向模仿：无尾的大猿，像猿一样照搬的动作，以及只会照搬的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big tailless ape, and a clumsy run at someone else's moves
core.cn: 核心意象：没有尾巴的大猿，以及照着别人动作硬学一遍

branches.en: A gorilla with no tail at all.
branches.cn: 完全没有尾巴的大猩猩。

branches.en: A gibbon swinging through the canopy.
branches.cn: 在树冠间摆荡的长臂猿。

branches.en: A chimp copying a keeper's wave.
branches.cn: 学饲养员挥手的小黑猩猩。

branches.en: A painter who only repeats others.
branches.cn: 只会重复别人的画家。

branches.en: Both copy without adding anything.
branches.cn: 两者都只是照搬，不加新东西。

intro.en: Ape itself has no affixes, but it takes -ish and -like, and the copying idea is carried by the Latin roots mim- and imit-.
intro.cn: ape 本身不带词缀，但可加 -ish 与 -like；「模仿」这一概念由拉丁词根 mim- 与 imit- 承载。

latinIntro.en: Ape is Germanic, so the classical layer belongs to its synonyms: Latin mimus and imitari, and similis for likeness.
latinIntro.cn: ape 是日耳曼词，所以古典层次属于它的近义词：拉丁语 mimus、imitari，以及表示相似的 similis。

definition_zh: 含糊其辞；支吾搪塞；两面讨好地说
definition_en: to use words that could mean two different things, deliberately avoiding a clear answer
core_image: 证席上一句话被劈成两半，左半承认右半否认，听者各自带走了想要的那一半
scene: 面对质问，部长一直含糊其辞。 The minister equivocated under questioning.
sceneCN: 这里 equivocate 是「含糊其辞」（第 1 个义项：有意让话可以两解）；句意：部长在追问下一味支吾。

pos.zh: 含糊其辞；支吾搪塞；两面讨好地说

collocations.zh: 在记录上口头上模棱两可

senses.title: To speak so a phrase carries two senses
senses.titleCN: 含糊其辞；模棱两可地说
senses.definition: to phrase a reply so that two interpretations remain open, usually on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把回答说得保留两种解释，通常是有意为之
senses.example: Witnesses equivocated for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 证人们含糊其辞了好几个小时。
senses.why: The Latin source names an equal voice, one that calls in two directions at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁源头说的是「声音相等」，即同时朝两个方向招呼。

senses.title: To deny in order to escape
senses.definition: to deny or hedge in order to avoid responsibility or a direct answer
senses.definitionCN: 为推卸责任或回避直答而否认或打折扣
senses.example: He equivocated about the money.
senses.exampleCN: 关于那笔钱他闪烁其词。
senses.why: Casuistry gave the word its moral edge, since evasion wore the mask of careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 决疑论给了它道德锋芒，因为回避常披上谨慎言辞的外衣。

senses.title: To use a term with two meanings in argument
senses.definition: a technical use in logic, switching between senses of one word inside a proof
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学专门用法，在同一论证中切换一个词的不同义
senses.example: The syllogism equivocated on law.
senses.exampleCN: 这段三段论在「规律」一词上偷换了概念。
senses.why: Textbooks of logic keep the fallacy named after the verb.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学教本保留了以该动词命名的谬误。

intro.en: Equivocate is built on late Latin aequivocare, from aequus equal plus vocare to call.
intro.cn: equivocate 建在晚期拉丁语 aequivocare 之上，由 aequus「相等」加 vocare「呼唤」构成。

items.en: Vocare means to call.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤。

items.en: Aequus means equal or level.
items.cn: aequus 意为相等、平坦。

items.en: Aequivocare means to call equally, so to share one name.
items.cn: aequivocare 意为同等地呼名，因而共有一名。

items.en: aequivocatio names terms with several senses.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 aequivocatio 指多义之名。

items.en: English takes the verb with a moral shading.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语摄入该动词并带道德色彩。

items.en: Religious controversy makes evasion its central sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪宗教论争把回避推为核心义。

note.en: Group one holds the vocare calling family; group two holds other verbs of evasive speech.
note.cn: 第一组是 vocare 这一表呼唤的词族；第二组是其他表回避性言辞的动词。

entries.definition: Open to two readings, describing a reply rather than a speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 可作两读，形容回答而非说话人。

entries.definition: Of the voice, from vocare.
entries.definitionCN: 与声音有关，出自 vocare。

entries.definition: To call on a name for help or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 呼名以求助或引权威。

entries.definition: To make equal, sharing the level prefix of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 使相等，与本词共享表平的词头。

entries.definition: To speak falsely so as to mislead, more formal than equivocate.
entries.definitionCN: 说假话以误导，比 equivocate 更书面。

entries.definition: To qualify a statement so it cannot be pinned down.
entries.definitionCN: 为陈述加限制使其无法被钉住。

entries.definition: To avoid committing in order to buy time.
entries.definitionCN: 不表态以拖延时间。

entries.definition: To make language dark on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 故意把话说得晦涩。

normalIntro.en: Equivocal describes the words; equivocate describes the speaker doing it.
normalIntro.cn: equivocal 形容话语，equivocate 说说话的人。

normal.en: Follow with about, on, or over, not with a that-clause.
normal.cn: 后接 about、on 或 over，不接 that 从句。

normal.en: Journalists use it when a refusal is dressed as an answer.
normal.cn: 当拒绝被包装成回答时，记者用这个词。

normal.en: The noun equivocation is more common in law reports.
normal.cn: 法律报道中更常用名词 equivocation。

normal.en: In logic it names a fallacy, not dishonesty.
normal.cn: 在逻辑学中它命名一种谬误而非不诚实。

normal.en: Keep stress on the second syllable of the first foot.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音步的第二音节上。

abstract.en: Picture an umpire who says both players could be right.
abstract.cn: 想象一位说两名球员都不错的裁判。

abstract.en: Imagine a sentence with a door on each end.
abstract.cn: 想象一句两端各开一门的句子。

abstract.en: Think of a witness who answers questions with weather reports.
abstract.cn: 想想那位用谈天气来回应提问的证人。

examples.en: The minister equivocated until the chair cut him off.
examples.cn: 部长一味含糊其辞，直到主席打断他。

examples.en: Equivocating about dates helped no one in the inquiry.
examples.cn: 在日期上支吾搪塞对调查毫无助益。

examples.en: One equivocated term can sink a whole proof.
examples.cn: 一个两可的概念就能拖垮整个证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一鬼滑腔」——话里带鬼、腔调打滑，所以 equivocate 是含糊其辞、支吾搪塞；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（相等）＋ vocare（呼唤）→ aequivocare（同名异实）→ 晚期拉丁 aequivocatio（多义）→ 英语 equivocate，核心义「一个名字朝两个方向呼唤」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers deliberate ambiguity, evasive denial, and a named fallacy in logic.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词涵盖存意的两可、回避式的否认，以及逻辑学中命名的一种谬误。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one name called out so it lands on two different things.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被喊出，同时落在两样不同的东西上。

branches.en: The speaker leaves both readings alive.
branches.cn: 说话人让两种解释都活着。

branches.en: Purpose turns ambiguity into escape.
branches.cn: 意图把两可变成脱身。

branches.en: Logic records the same move as a defect.
branches.cn: 逻辑学把同一手法记为缺陷。

branches.en: Both turn on a word with two senses.
branches.cn: 两者都系于一个多义之词。

branches.en: Both belong to speech under pressure.
branches.cn: 两者都属于压力之下的言说。

intro.en: A stem of levelness joins a stem of calling, and a frequentative ending makes the verb.
intro.cn: 表平等的词干接上表呼唤的词干，再以动频词尾构成动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare is to call, vocare nomen is to name, and aequare is to make equal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare 表呼唤，vocare nomen 表命名，aequare 表使相等。

items.example: A plain cousin on the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干上朴素的表亲词。

latinEntries.meaning: to call by the same name

definition_zh: adj. 秃头的；无发的；光秃的、磨平的；（陈述）直白的、不加掩饰的
definition_en: having little or no hair on the scalp; lacking natural covering or detail; plain and blunt, without softening
core_image: 帽子摘下后那片反着光的头顶
scene: 他摘下帽子，露出光亮的前额。 He took off his cap and showed a bald crown that caught the light.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bald 指头上无发；句意是他摘帽后露出反光的秃顶。

pos.zh: 秃的；光秃的；直白的

senses.title: Without hair
senses.definition: having little or no hair on the head
senses.definitionCN: 头上很少或没有头发
senses.example: He went bald in his early thirties.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十出头就秃了。
senses.why: The Middle English form described a shining white patch on the head, and the sense narrowed to the bareness itself.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语形式描写头上一块发亮的白斑，词义后来收窄为「光秃」本身。

senses.title: Stripped of covering
senses.definition: lacking the natural or usual covering, such as hair, tread, or vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 缺少天然或惯常的覆盖物，如毛发、胎面花纹或植被
senses.example: The tyres were bald and the hillside was bare.
senses.exampleCN: 轮胎花纹磨平了，山坡也光秃秃的。
senses.why: Once bald means bare skin, any surface that has lost its layer can borrow the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然 bald 指裸露的皮肤，任何失去表层的表面都能借用这个词。

senses.title: Plain and blunt
senses.definition: stated without any attempt to soften or disguise it
senses.definitionCN: 陈述时不作任何缓和或掩饰
senses.example: It was a bald lie and everyone knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个赤裸裸的谎言，人人都看得出来。
senses.why: Speech with nothing laid over it is bare in the same way as a head with no hair.
senses.whyCN: 不加覆盖的言语，与不长头发的头一样「赤裸」。

intro.en: Bald probably began as a word about colour, not hair: a shining white patch. From there it moved to bareness, and then to blunt speech.
intro.cn: bald 起初大概是讲颜色而非头发：一块发亮的白斑。由此转为「光秃」，再转为「言语直白」。

items.en: The root bhel meant to shine or gleam white, and it also gives blaze and bleach.
items.cn: 词根 bhel 意为发亮或呈白色，也衍生出 blaze 与 bleach。

items.en: Middle English balled describes a head marked by a shining white patch.
items.cn: 中古英语 balled 形容头上有一块发亮的白斑。

items.en: Welsh bal names a white streak on the forehead of a horse, a close match in sense.
items.cn: 威尔士语 bal 指马额上的白色条纹，词义十分接近。

items.en: The spelling settles as bald, and the meaning shifts from white patch to hairless.
items.cn: 拼写定为 bald，词义由「白斑」转为「无发」。

items.en: Writers use the word for any surface stripped of its natural cover, such as a bald hill.
items.cn: 文人用该词指任何失去天然覆盖的表面，如光秃的山丘。

items.en: A figurative sense grows: the word now marks a statement left blunt and unsoftened.
items.cn: 又生出比喻义：该词指陈述直白、不加缓和修饰。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on one-letter and one-vowel neighbours, bold above all; the near-meaning group splits into bare surfaces and blunt speech, matching the two extended senses.
note.cn: 形近组由只差一个字母或一个元音的邻居组成，尤其是 bold；近义组分为「裸露表面」与「言语直白」两支，正对应两个引申义。

entries.definition: Confident and willing to take risks.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；无畏的。

entries.definition: A round object used in games.
entries.definitionCN: 球；圆球状物。

entries.definition: A large bound bundle of hay or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 一大捆干草或废纸。

entries.definition: To shout or weep noisily.
entries.definitionCN: 大喊；号哭。

entries.definition: Having no hair on a normally hairy part.
entries.definitionCN: 本应有毛处无毛的。

entries.definition: Without covering or clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 裸露的；无遮盖的。

entries.definition: With hair removed by a razor.
entries.definitionCN: 剃过的；刮净的。

entries.definition: Direct in speech, sometimes rudely so.
entries.definitionCN: 说话直率的，有时近于无礼。

normalIntro.en: Bald and bold differ by one vowel: bold is a full head of courage, bald is an empty head of hair.
normalIntro.cn: bald 与 bold 只差一个元音：bold 是满头勇气，bald 是满头无发。

normal.en: See the a in bald and think of a bare scalp.
normal.cn: 看到 bald 里的 a，就想一片空空的头皮。

normal.en: A bald tyre has lost its tread, just as a head loses hair.
normal.cn: bald tyre 是花纹磨光的轮胎，正如头掉了头发。

normal.en: A bald statement has no covering words.
normal.cn: bald statement 是没有修饰词遮盖的陈述。

normal.en: Balder and baldest are the regular comparisons.
normal.cn: 比较级 balder、最高级 baldest 都是规则变化。

normal.en: Baldness is the state, baldly is the manner.
normal.cn: baldness 是状态，baldly 是方式。

abstract.en: A surface with nothing left to hide behind.
abstract.cn: 一个再无遮蔽可依的表面。

abstract.en: Truth without its usual coat.
abstract.cn: 没穿惯常外衣的真话。

abstract.en: Time taking away a layer nobody asked it to take.
abstract.cn: 时间取走了一层谁也没让它取的东西。

examples.en: His bald head shone under the office lights.
examples.cn: 他的秃头在办公室灯下发亮。

examples.en: The report gave a bald account of the losses.
examples.cn: 报告对损失作了毫不掩饰的陈述。

examples.en: Bald patches appeared where the sheep had grazed.
examples.cn: 羊啃过的地方出现了一块块秃斑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 对比记忆：bold「大胆」把 o 换成 a 就成了 bald「秃的」——胆子鼓鼓是 bold，头顶空空是 bald。再串三层：头顶无发 → 表面无覆盖 → 说话无修饰。

root: 可能源自原始印欧语词根 bhel「发亮、白」，中古英语约 1300 年作 balled，指头上发亮的白斑；威尔士语 bal「马额白纹」为旁证。15 世纪拼写定为 bald 并转指无发，17 世纪扩为一切光秃表面，19 世纪再扩为言语直白。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses, one idea: a surface with its covering gone, whether that covering is hair, tread, or polite wording.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项，一个念头：覆盖物消失后的表面——不论那覆盖物是头发、胎面花纹，还是客套的措辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cap lifted off a shining bare crown
core.cn: 核心意象：帽子从反光的秃顶上被揭开

branches.en: A razor drawn over the scalp.
branches.cn: 剃刀刮过头皮。

branches.en: A tyre worn smooth to the casing.
branches.cn: 磨到露出胎体的光轮胎。

branches.en: A hillside cropped to the soil.
branches.cn: 啃到露土的山坡。

branches.en: A lie with no wrapper.
branches.cn: 没有包装的谎言。

branches.en: Nothing left on top.
branches.cn: 上面什么也不剩。

intro.en: Bald is a bare adjective root; the useful endings are the comparison pair and the suffixes that turn it into a state or a manner.
intro.cn: bald 是一个赤裸的形容词词根；有用的词尾是比较级最高级这一对，以及把它变成状态或方式的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the learned synonyms rather than the word itself: calvus for bald and glaber for smooth and hairless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供的是书面近义表达而非该词本身：calvus 表「秃」，glaber 表「光滑无毛」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: Calvus 曾是罗马人的绰号。

definition_zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；挥发气体；幻想之物
definition_en: a substance in its gaseous state, especially one given off by a liquid or solid, or a faint mist
core_image: 一滴汽油落在热石头上，转眼化成一缕看不见的气，散进空气
scene: 加油站的地面上洒了一点汽油，太阳晒过后空气里浮起一层薄薄的气。 Petrol vapor drifted across the forecourt until the warning sign was moved closer.
sceneCN: 这里指「由液体挥发出来的气体」（第 1 个义项：液体或固体变成的气态物质）；句意为汽油蒸气飘过加油场地，直到警告牌被移近。图中可辨识物件：加油机、湿地面、浮起的气层、警告牌。

pos.zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；挥发气体

senses.title: A substance given off as gas
senses.titleCN: 由液体或固体发出的气态物质
senses.definition: the gaseous form of a substance that has passed off from a liquid or solid
senses.definitionCN: 由液体或固体散出后形成的气态物质
senses.example: Petrol vapor drifted across the forecourt until the warning sign was moved closer.
senses.exampleCN: 汽油蒸气飘过加油场地，直到警告牌被移近。
senses.why: Latin vapor named steam and exhalation, so the English word starts from what rises off a warm surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vapor 指蒸汽与呼出的气，因此英语这个词从「自温热表面升腾而起的东西」出发。

senses.title: Water as an invisible gas
senses.definition: gaseous water, whether in the air or above a warm surface
senses.definitionCN: 处于气态的水，无论在空气中还是在温热表面上方的水
senses.example: The vapour above the kettle is water, not smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 壶上方的气是水汽，不是烟。
senses.why: The commonest vapor in daily life is water, so the word is regularly used without naming the substance.
senses.whyCN: 日常最常见的蒸气就是水，因此这个词常单独使用而不必点明物质。

senses.title: A faint visible mist
senses.definition: a thin mist or cloud of condensed droplets that can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 由凝结液滴构成、能被看见的薄雾或气团
senses.example: A cold vapor hung over the hot spring at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时温泉上方挂着一层冷雾。
senses.why: Visible vapour is already part liquid, but English kept one word for both the invisible gas and the mist it makes.
senses.whyCN: 可见的蒸气其实已含液态，但英语用同一个词兼指看不见的气与它形成的雾。

senses.title: The gas phase in chemistry
senses.definition: the gaseous phase of a substance studied apart from its liquid or solid phase
senses.definitionCN: 物质的气相，与液相、固相并列研究
senses.example: The vapour above the solvent reached equilibrium with the liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 溶剂上方的气相与液相达到平衡。
senses.why: Laboratory usage turned the everyday word into a name for one phase in a system of phases.
senses.whyCN: 实验室用法把这个日常词变成物相体系中的一个相名。

senses.title: Fumes from fuel or solvent
senses.titleCN: 燃料或溶剂挥发的气体
senses.definition: the flammable or harmful gas given off by a fuel, solvent or chemical
senses.definitionCN: 燃料、溶剂或化学品散出的易燃或有毒气体
senses.example: Vapour from the tank collected under the shed roof.
senses.exampleCN: 罐中散出的蒸气聚集在棚顶下。
senses.why: Industry applied the word to whatever a liquid gives off, and with it came the language of risk.
senses.whyCN: 工业界用这个词指液体散出的一切气体，随之而来的是风险的语言。

senses.title: The aerosol from an e-cigarette
senses.definition: the cloud exhaled from a device that heats a liquid rather than burning tobacco
senses.definitionCN: 由加热液体、而非燃烧烟草的装置呼出的气团
senses.example: A sweet vapor filled the shop's tasting room.
senses.exampleCN: 一股甜味气雾充满店里的试抽室。
senses.why: The newer use stretches the word to a cloud that is mostly droplets, because it looks and behaves like vapour.
senses.whyCN: 较新的用法把这个词扩展到以液滴为主的气团，因为它看上去、动起来都像蒸气。

senses.title: The old medical 'vapours'
senses.titleCN: 旧时医学所说的「体内之气」
senses.definition: in older medicine, exhalations believed to rise from the body and cause low spirits
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学认为自体内升起、引起情绪低落的气
senses.example: The eighteenth-century letter blamed her melancholy on the vapours.
senses.exampleCN: 这封十八世纪的书信把她的忧郁归因于体内之气。
senses.why: Before physiology, illness was often explained by rising vapours, and the plural became a name for melancholy itself.
senses.whyCN: 在生理学之前，疾病常被解释为上升的气，复数形式遂成为「忧郁」的代称。

senses.title: Something without substance
senses.definition: something imagined, insubstantial or without practical effect
senses.definitionCN: 想象出来的、没有实体或没有实际作用的东西
senses.example: The promise turned out to be vapor and nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 那个承诺到头来只是空话。
senses.why: What has no body and cannot be grasped became the natural image for a claim with no substance.
senses.whyCN: 没有形体、抓不住的东西，自然成了「没有实质的主张」的意象。

intro.en: Vapor comes from Latin vapor 'steam, exhalation, warmth', through Old French. It entered English in the late fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vapor 经古法语来自拉丁 vapor「蒸汽、呼气、热」，在十四世纪末进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vapor covered steam, breath and warmth, and could also mean a light exhalation rising from the ground. The word was used in both everyday and medical writing.
items.cn: vapor 兼指蒸汽、呼吸与热，也可指从地面升起的轻气。这个词在日常写作与医学写作中都出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): vapor has no established pre-Latin origin. Suggestions linking it to vapidus 'flat, spoiled' or to a Greek form are hypotheses, not proven derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：vapor 没有已确定的拉丁语之前来源。把它与 vapidus「走味的、败坏的」或某个希腊形式相联系的说法都是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French vapour carried the noun into English, where the spelling vapor later became standard in American use.
items.cn: 古法语 vapour 把这个名词带入英语，后来 vapor 这一拼写成为美式标准。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the plural vapours named a condition of low spirits, thought to arise from exhalations within the body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，复数 the vapours 指一种情绪低落的状态，时人认为它源于体内升起的气。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics fixed vapor as a technical term for the gas phase of a substance below its critical temperature.
items.cn: 十九世纪的物理学把 vapor 固定为术语，指低于临界温度时物质的气相。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries added fuel vapour, vapour trails and the aerosol of vaping, all extensions of the same visible or invisible cloud.
items.cn: 二十与二十一世纪又添出燃料蒸气、凝结尾迹与电子烟气雾，都是同一种可见或不可见气团的延伸。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word or its near-homographs; group two holds the physical neighbours of vapour in the air.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式或近形词；第二组是空气中和蒸气相邻的物理概念。

entries.definition: The identical word in British spelling; only the orthography differs.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，只有正字法不同。

entries.definition: From vapidus 'flat, spoiled', used of drinks and later of dull talk; it is not a form of vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 vapidus「走味的、败坏的」，先用于饮料，后指乏味的言谈；并非 vapor 的词形变化。

entries.definition: e- 'out' plus vaporare: to pass off as vapour, the action rather than the substance.
entries.definitionCN: e-「向外」加 vaporare：以蒸气形式散失，是动作而非物质。

entries.definition: A device that turns a liquid into vapour or spray; the machine, not the gas.
entries.definitionCN: 把液体变成蒸气或喷雾的装置；指机器而非气体。

entries.definition: The hot vapour produced by boiling water, often visible; vapor is the wider term for any gaseous substance.
entries.definitionCN: 沸水产生的热蒸气，常可见；vapor 是泛指任何气态物质的更宽的词。

entries.definition: A suspension of tiny liquid droplets; it is already condensed, while vapour may still be a true gas.
entries.definitionCN: 微小液滴的悬浮体，已经凝结；而 vapor 仍可能是真正的气体。

entries.definition: A gas or smoke that is unpleasant or harmful, usually from a chemical process; vapor is neutral about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不适或有害的气体或烟，通常来自化学过程；vapor 对是否有害保持中立。

entries.definition: The general word for any substance in the gaseous state; vapor is usual for gas given off by a liquid or solid.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何气态物质的通用词；vapor 通常指由液体或固体散出的气体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin vapor meant steam and breath, so anything that rises off a warm surface is a vapor.
normal.cn: 拉丁 vapor 意为蒸汽与呼气，因此从温热表面升起的东西都可称 vapor。

normal.en: The family runs vaporize, vaporization, vaporizer, vaporous and evaporate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 vaporize、vaporization、vaporizer、vaporous 与 evaporate。

normal.en: Technical phrases mark the science: vapor pressure, vapor phase, vapor trail.
normal.cn: 技术搭配标出科学义：蒸气压、气相、凝结尾迹。

normal.en: American spelling is vapor; British spelling is vapour, the same word twice.
normal.cn: 美式拼作 vapor，英式拼作 vapour，是同一个词的两种写法。

normal.en: Vapour is invisible as a gas and visible only once it condenses into droplets.
normal.cn: 作为气体时蒸气看不见，一旦凝结成液滴才可见。

abstract.en: Picture a coin left in the sun until nothing solid remains in your hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币晒在太阳下，手里最后什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written on a window that fogs and then clears.
abstract.cn: 想象写在窗上的承诺，起雾又散去。

abstract.en: Picture a breath you can see for a second on a winter morning.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日清晨一口能看见一瞬的呼气。

examples.en: Fuel vapor ignites if a spark reaches the tank vent.
examples.cn: 火花触及油箱通气口时，燃料蒸气会被点燃。

examples.en: The vapour above the solvent was vented through a scrubber.
examples.cn: 溶剂上方的蒸气经洗涤器排出。

examples.en: His plans proved to be vapor once the funding was checked.
examples.cn: 资金一核对，他的计划便成了空话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vapor 听起来像『微泼』」——水一泼到热处就化成气 → 蒸气

root: 拉丁 vapor「蒸汽、呼气、热」，经古法语 vapour 进入英语；vapor 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，与 vapidus「走味的」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising cloud: it is gas given off by matter, it is water, it is a visible mist, it is a phase, it is fuel fume, it is aerosol, it was once a name for melancholy, and at last it is anything with no substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一团升起的气展开：它是物质散出的气体，是水，是可见的雾，是一个物相，是燃料气，是气雾，曾是忧郁的代称，最后指一切没有实质之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop on hot stone turning into a curl of gas too fine to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：热石上的一滴水化作一缕细得看不见的气。

branches.en: PLAIN SUBSTANCE: water or petrol, the gas comes off a liquid.
branches.cn: 基本物质：无论是水还是汽油，气体都自液体散出。

branches.en: VISIBLE CLOUD: once droplets form, the vapour can be seen.
branches.cn: 可见的气团：液滴一旦形成，蒸气便看得见。

branches.en: ONE PHASE: chemistry names the gas phase beside liquid and solid.
branches.cn: 一个物相：化学把气相与液相、固相并列命名。

branches.en: RISK AND DEVICE: fuel fumes and the aerosol of a heated liquid both fill a space.
branches.cn: 风险与装置：燃料气与加热液体产生的气雾都会充满空间。

branches.en: NO BODY: the old humours and the empty promise share the same thinness.
branches.cn: 没有形体：旧时的体液说与空洞的承诺共享同一种稀薄。

intro.en: Vapor is a Latin noun whose stem builds a whole family of English words for turning into gas and for misty appearance.
intro.cn: vapor 是拉丁名词，其词干在英语中构成一整套表示「变成气体」与「雾状外观」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor and vaporare give vapor, vaporous, evaporate and evaporation; -ize and -izer are living English suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 与 vaporare 衍生 vapor、vaporous、evaporate 与 evaporation；-ize 与 -izer 是仍在使用的英语后缀。

items.example: A vapour rose from the spring.
The hot stone steamed in the rain.
The valley was vaporous at sunrise.
A vaporous haze hung over the town.
items.exampleCN: 一层雾状的薄霭罩着小镇。

definition_zh: 使困窘；使羞愧；使局促不安
definition_en: to make someone feel embarrassed, ashamed, or uncomfortable
core_image: 一句当众戳破的话，让人的脸瞬间红透、手足无措
scene: 她在讨论会上被老师当众点名回答难题。 The unexpected question abashed her in front of the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 abash 是「使困窘」（第 1 个义项：令人当众难堪）；句意为一个出其不意的问题让她在全班面前局促不安。

pos.zh: 使困窘；使羞愧
使局促不安（常用过去分词 abashed）

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转作形容词，义为「窘迫的；局促不安的」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不害臊的；毫不羞愧的」

senses.title: To embarrass someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel embarrassed or awkward, especially in public
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到尴尬或难堪，尤指当众
senses.example: The teacher's sudden praise abashed the shy student.
senses.exampleCN: 老师突如其来的表扬让害羞的学生窘迫起来。
senses.why: Old French esba- carried the idea of striking someone wide and open; a sudden blow to the face makes the cheeks burn.
senses.whyCN: 古法语词干带有「猛然打开放倒」的意味；突袭式的一击会让人脸上发烫。

senses.title: To shame someone into silence
senses.definition: to make a person feel so ashamed or small that they stop speaking or acting
senses.definitionCN: 使人感到羞愧或渺小，以致停止说话或行动
senses.example: Her cold logic abashed the loudest debater into silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷静的逻辑使那位最吵的辩手羞愧语塞。
senses.why: Shame presses the mouth shut; the embarrassment of the first sense deepens into a shame that ends the exchange.
senses.whyCN: 羞愧把嘴压上；第一义的尴尬加深为一种让交流终止的羞耻。

senses.title: To unsettle someone's composure
senses.definition: to disturb someone's confidence or composure, even without a public audience
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某人的自信或镇定，即使并无旁观者
senses.example: The strange smile on the portrait abashed every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 画像上那抹怪异的微笑使每位访客都心神不定。
senses.why: The same blow can land inside: confidence is knocked open and off balance, whether or not anyone is watching.
senses.whyCN: 同样的一击也可以落在心里：自信被击开、失衡，无论有无旁观者。

intro.en: Abash descends from an Anglo-French verb meaning to strike open or throw into confusion, built on a root meaning to gape.
intro.cn: abash 源自盎格鲁-法语动词「猛击使张口、使人混乱」，其词根意为「张大口」。

items.en: A Frankish root for gaping or yawning is reconstructed behind the French verb.
items.cn: 法语动词背后重构出一个法兰克语词根，意为张口、打哈欠。

items.en: Esbaer meant to gape in wonder or be struck open with astonishment.
items.cn: 古法语 esbaer 意为惊讶地张口，或被惊得敞开。

items.en: Abaiss-, used in England, took the sense of confounding or striking with shame.
items.cn: 在英格兰使用的盎格鲁-法语形式 abaisse 转指使人混乱、使人蒙羞。

items.en: Abashen appeared with the meaning to make ashamed.
items.cn: 中古英语 abashen 出现，意为使人羞愧。

items.en: The verb survives mostly in the participle abashed and its negative unabashed.
items.cn: 该动词如今主要存于分词 abashed 及其否定式 unabashed。

note.en: Abash is often confused with abase, though the two come from different French verbs.
note.cn: abash 常与 abase 混淆，二者虽词尾相近，却来自不同的法语动词。

entries.definition: to lower someone's dignity, not their composure
entries.definitionCN: 贬低某人的身份尊严，而非使其窘迫；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the participle meaning embarrassed
entries.definitionCN: 分词形式，义为窘迫的

entries.definition: not embarrassed, openly confident
entries.definitionCN: 加 un- 的否定形式，义为不害臊的

entries.definition: to make someone feel awkward
entries.definitionCN: 使人尴尬；语域更日常

entries.definition: to cause someone strong shame
entries.definitionCN: 使人深感羞辱；程度重于 abash

entries.definition: to unsettle or thwart someone
entries.definitionCN: 使人心神不安；语域更书面

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abash to the burning face.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abash 和发烫的脸绑在一起。

normal.en: a- + bash: like being smacked, the face burns.
normal.cn: a- ＋ bash（像挨了一巴掌）：脸瞬间发烫。

normal.en: abashed describes the red-cheeked state.
normal.cn: abashed 形容两颊发红的状态。

normal.en: unabashed: not red at all, shameless and calm.
normal.cn: unabashed：毫不脸红，坦然自若。

normal.en: Contrast abase: rank goes down, only cheeks burn here.
normal.cn: 对比 abase：那边是身份下降，这边只是脸红。

normal.en: Think of bashful, a cousin feeling of shyness.
normal.cn: 联想 bashful「害羞的」，情绪近亲。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight snapping on at a bad moment.
abstract.cn: 想象难堪时刻聚光灯骤然亮起。

abstract.en: Feel the floor vanish under a too-big applause.
abstract.cn: 感到掌声过大时脚下地板消失。

abstract.en: See mouths gaping open in one stunned room.
abstract.cn: 看见满屋人张口结舌的样子。

examples.en: Nothing could abash her once she decided to speak.
examples.cn: 一旦决定开口，什么都无法让她窘迫退缩。

examples.en: He stood abashed by his own careless words.
examples.cn: 他被自己无心的话弄得窘迫不已。

examples.en: The truth abashed the liar in front of the crowd.
examples.cn: 真相使说谎者在众人面前羞愧难当。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅被嘘」——鹅被全场嘘了一声，红着脸不敢作声

root: 一般认为源自古法语 esbaer「惊愕张口」＝ es-（出自拉丁 ex-「向外」）＋ baer「张大口」（日耳曼语源，与 gape 之源相关）。经盎格鲁-法语进入中古英语 abashen。词根部分属重构形式，学者意见不一。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses widen one blow: from public embarrassment to shaming silence to inner unrest.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项扩展同一次「击打」：从当众难堪，到羞得语塞，再到内心不安。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sudden strike opens the face and the room stares.
core.cn: 核心意象：猛然一击，脸被打开，满屋目光落在上面。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC BLOW: embarrassment before an audience.
branches.cn: 当众一击：在旁观者面前的尴尬。

branches.en: THE DEEPENED BLOW: shame closes the mouth.
branches.cn: 加深的一击：羞愧让嘴闭上。

branches.en: THE INNER BLOW: composure shakes with no crowd needed.
branches.cn: 内心一击：无需观众，镇定也为之动摇。

branches.en: FACE BEFORE OTHERS: both senses need the eyes of others.
branches.cn: 人前的脸：这两个义项都依赖他人的目光。

branches.en: ONE STRIKE, THREE DEPTHS: skin, mouth, mind.
branches.cn: 一击三重：皮肤、嘴巴、心神。

intro.en: The frame is French with an ex- prefix, while the inner root is Germanic.
intro.cn: 框架是法语的，带 ex- 类前缀，而内部词根来自日耳曼语。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex- contributes the French es-, but the gaping root itself is a Germanic reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex- 提供了法语 es-，但「张口」词根本身属日耳曼语重构形式。

items.example: It is the heart of esbaer.
It gives the sense of being struck open.
items.exampleCN: 它给出被击得敞开的意味。
它与 bash- 的情绪同族。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「窘迫的」
加 un- 构成，义为「不害臊的」

definition_zh: 有选择性的；挑拣严格的；选择性的（只影响特定对象的）；选择吸附的
definition_en: choosing carefully, or affecting only particular members of a group rather than all of them
core_image: 一把筛子只让某一种颗粒落下，其余的被留在上面
scene: 这里指「有选择性的」。 The herbicide is selective: it kills the weeds but leaves the crop standing.
sceneCN: 这里 selective 指「只影响特定对象的」（第 3 个义项：作用范围限于某类对象而非全部）；除草剂杀杂草而不伤作物。图中可辨识物件：喷雾器、杂草、作物、筛状示意。

pos.zh: 有选择性的；挑拣严格的；只影响特定对象的（比较级 more selective，最高级 most selective）

senses.title: Choosing with care
senses.definition: careful in what one chooses or accepts
senses.definitionCN: 在选择或接受时十分谨慎
senses.example: She is selective about the films she reviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己评论的影片挑得很严。
senses.why: The suffix -ive on select makes an adjective of tendency: a person or body that tends to pick rather than take everything.
senses.whyCN: select 加后缀 -ive 构成倾向性形容词：倾向于挑选而非全盘接受的人或机构。

senses.title: Hard to get into
senses.titleCN: 录取门槛高：只收少数人
senses.definition: admitting only a small proportion of applicants
senses.definitionCN: 只录取申请者中的一小部分
senses.example: The programme is one of the most selective in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目是全国录取门槛最高的之一。
senses.why: Institutions narrow the sense: the picking becomes a filter on applicants, and selectivity turns into prestige.
senses.whyCN: 建制把词义收窄：挑选变成了对申请者的筛子，选择性于是转化为声望。

senses.title: Affecting only a target
senses.titleCN: 只作用于特定对象：不波及全体
senses.definition: acting on a particular kind of thing and leaving others untouched
senses.definitionCN: 只作用于某一类事物，不影响其他事物
senses.example: A selective drug lowers the heart rate without dulling the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 一种选择性药物能降低心率而不使头脑迟钝。
senses.why: Pharmacology and chemistry sharpened the word: selectivity is measured by how narrowly the effect lands.
senses.whyCN: 药理学与化学把这个词磨得更锋利：选择性以作用范围有多窄来衡量。

senses.title: Selective memory
senses.titleCN: 选择性记忆：只记住合意的部分
senses.definition: remembering some events and conveniently forgetting others
senses.definitionCN: 记住某些事件而便利地忘记另一些
senses.example: His selective memory lost every promise he had made.
senses.exampleCN: 他的选择性记忆把他许过的承诺全都丢了。
senses.why: The filter image moves into the mind: memory keeps only what suits, as if it had a screen.
senses.whyCN: 筛子意象移入心智：记忆只留下合意的部分，仿佛自带筛网。

senses.title: Selective breeding
senses.titleCN: 选择性繁育：按目标性状留种
senses.definition: breeding plants or animals only from individuals that show desired traits
senses.definitionCN: 只用表现出所需性状的个体进行繁育
senses.example: Selective breeding produced a wheat that ripens early.
senses.exampleCN: 选择性繁育培育出一种早熟小麦。
senses.why: The human chooser returns here, matching artificial selection: each generation is picked by a criterion.
senses.whyCN: 此处人类选择者回归，与人工选择相呼应：每一代都按某个标准被挑过。

senses.title: Selective pressure
senses.titleCN: 选择压力：环境只留下适应的变异
senses.definition: a force in the environment that favours some variants over others
senses.definitionCN: 环境中偏爱某些变异、淘汰另一些变异的力量
senses.example: Drought is a selective pressure on root depth.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱对根深构成一种选择压力。
senses.why: The adjective marks the unevenness: some variants survive the filter, and the unevenness is called pressure.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标出这种不均衡：有些变异通过了筛子，这种不均衡就被称为压力。

senses.title: Selective absorption
senses.titleCN: 选择性吸收：只吸收特定波段
senses.definition: in physics and chemistry, taking up only certain wavelengths or substances
senses.definitionCN: 物理与化学中指只吸收某些波长或某些物质
senses.example: Ozone shows strong selective absorption in the ultraviolet.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧在紫外波段表现出强烈的选择性吸收。
senses.why: Spectroscopy measures the narrowness of a response, and the everyday filter image becomes a precise technical property.
senses.whyCN: 光谱学测量响应的狭窄程度，日常的筛子意象于是变成了精确的技术属性。

senses.title: Selective in communication
senses.titleCN: 有选择地传达：只说一部分
senses.definition: giving information only to certain people or only in part
senses.definitionCN: 只向某些人、或只按部分内容提供信息
senses.example: He was selective in what he told the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他向委员会汇报时有所选择。
senses.why: The word moves from things to speech: a speaker filters the message, releasing only part of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物转到言语：说话者过滤信息，只放出一部分。

intro.en: Selective is an English adjective built on the Latin participle selectus, from seligere 'to choose out' (se- 'apart' + legere 'to pick'). The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: selective 是英语形容词，建立在拉丁分词 selectus 之上，后者出自 seligere「挑出」（se-「分开」+ legere「挑选」）。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: The past participle selectus 'chosen out' supplied English with select, and the participle also underlies the adjective. The root verb legere meant 'to gather, pick, read'.
items.cn: 过去分词 selectus「被挑出的」为英语提供了 select，该分词同样是形容词的基础。词根动词 legere 意为「收集、挑选、阅读」。

items.en: English formed adjectives of tendency with -ive, from Latin -ivus. Selective therefore means 'having the tendency to select', not merely 'having been selected'.
items.cn: 英语用 -ive（源自拉丁 -ivus）构成倾向性形容词。因此 selective 意为「有挑选倾向的」，而不只是「被选中的」。

items.en: The word spread with the growth of breeding, chemistry and electrical engineering, where the question was always how narrowly an effect could be aimed. The earliest technical uses are uncertain in date.
items.cn: 随着育种、化学与电气工程的发展，这个词流行开来，而这些领域关心的始终是「效果能被瞄得多准」。最早的技术用法年代存疑。

items.en: Selective became ordinary in education and medicine: selective schools, selective drugs, selective memory. Each kept the filter image.
items.cn: 20 世纪 selective 在教育与医学中成为常用词：择优学校、选择性药物、选择性记忆。每一处都保留了筛子的意象。

items.en: Today the word is chiefly contrastive: it always implies that some members are passed over, which is why it so often appears beside 'only' or 'not all'.
items.cn: 今天这个词主要用于对比：它总暗含有些成员被略过，这正是它常与 only、not all 同现的原因。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English citation of selective is usually placed in the nineteenth century but is not firmly fixed; the deep origin of legere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：selective 的英语首见书证通常定在 19 世纪，但并不确凿；legere 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group holds same-family adjectives that are easily swapped by mistake; the second holds near-synonyms about choosing or limiting.
note.cn: 第一组是同族形容词，容易被误换；第二组是表示挑选或限定的近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'chosen' after the fact. Selective means having the habit or power of choosing, so the two cannot be swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「事后被选中的」。selective 意为具备挑选的习惯或能力，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: The act of choosing or the chosen set; it cannot modify a noun the way selective does.
entries.definitionCN: 指挑选动作或被选中之物；它不能像 selective 那样修饰名词。

entries.definition: As a verb it names the action; as an adjective it means 'of high quality and restricted access', a narrower sense than selective.
entries.definitionCN: 作动词时命名动作；作形容词时意为「精选而门槛高的」，比 selective 的义域更窄。

entries.definition: Means 'chosen by the voter' or 'optional', as in an elective course. It shares legere but says nothing about filtering.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「由选举产生的」或「选修的」，如 elective course。它同出 legere，但与筛选无关。

entries.definition: Showing refined judgment in taste. It praises discernment, while selective may merely describe a filter.
entries.definitionCN: 在品味上表现出精细判断。它称赞鉴别力，而 selective 可能只是描述一个筛子。

entries.definition: Restricted to a privileged few. Selective stresses the act of filtering; exclusive stresses who is kept out.
entries.definitionCN: 限于少数特权者。selective 强调筛选动作，exclusive 强调被排除在外的对象。

entries.definition: Directed at a specific group or place. It stresses aim, while selective stresses the narrowness of effect.
entries.definitionCN: 针对特定群体或地点。它强调瞄准，而 selective 强调效果范围的狭窄。

entries.definition: Clearly defined or particular. A specific drug is named exactly; a selective drug is one that acts narrowly.
entries.definitionCN: 明确界定或特定的。specific 的药是被精确命名的，selective 的药是作用范围窄的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: select + -ive: the suffix marks a tendency, so selective is 'given to picking'.
normal.cn: select + -ive：后缀标记倾向，故 selective 是「惯于挑选的」。

normal.en: The family runs select, selected, selection, selective, selectively, selectivity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 select、selected、selection、selective、selectively、selectivity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: selective breeding, selective memory, selective admission, highly selective.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：选择性繁育、选择性记忆、择优录取、门槛极高。

normal.en: The core contrast is 'some, not all', which is why the word pairs naturally with only.
normal.cn: 核心对比是「部分而非全部」，因此这个词天然与 only 搭配。

normal.en: selected is the result; selective is the habit or the narrow aim.
normal.cn: selected 是结果；selective 是习惯或狭窄的作用范围。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve tilted so that only one size of grain falls through.
abstract.cn: 想象一只斜放的筛子，只让一种大小的谷粒落下。

abstract.en: Picture a doorman who checks one list and waves most people past.
abstract.cn: 想象一名门卫只核对一张名单，把大多数人挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp with a narrow beam that leaves the rest of the room untouched.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏窄光束的灯，房间其余部分不受影响。

examples.en: The university is highly selective, admitting fewer than one in ten applicants.
examples.cn: 这所大学录取门槛极高，十个申请者中录取不到一个。

examples.en: Selective grazing changed which grasses survived in the meadow.
examples.cn: 选择性啃食改变了草甸中哪些草得以存活。

examples.en: He gave a selective account of the meeting, leaving out his own errors.
examples.cn: 他对会议作了有选择的叙述，略去了自己的失误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「select（挑）+ ive（爱……的）」——爱挑的 → selective 有选择性的、只挑一部分的

root: 拉丁 legere「收集、挑选」→ seligere「挑出」→ selectus → 英语 select + -ive → selective。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one filter: a screen lets part of a group through, and the word can describe a careful person, a strict school, a narrow drug, a partial memory or a biased account.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一只筛子展开：筛网让群体的一部分通过，这个词既可描述谨慎的人、门槛高的学校、作用窄的药物，也可描述有偏的记忆或不完整的叙述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve that passes one kind of grain and holds the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只筛子只放过某一种颗粒，其余留在上面。

branches.en: THE PICKER: the adjective of tendency, describing someone careful about what they accept.
branches.cn: 挑选者：倾向性形容词，描述对接受之物十分谨慎的人。

branches.en: THE THRESHOLD: institutions convert picking into admission rules and prestige.
branches.cn: 门槛：建制把挑选转化为录取规则与声望。

branches.en: NARROW AIM: pharmacology and spectroscopy measure how tightly an effect is confined.
branches.cn: 瞄准狭窄：药理学与光谱学测量效果被约束得多紧。

branches.en: PARTIAL KEEPING: memory and speech release only part of what they hold.
branches.cn: 部分保留：记忆与言语只放出所持内容的一部分。

branches.en: BREEDING AND PRESSURE: a human or an environment applies the filter across generations.
branches.cn: 繁育与压力：人或环境跨世代地施加这只筛子。

intro.en: Selective is a Latin participle stem plus an English tendency suffix, with the separation prefix se- at the front.
intro.cn: selective 是拉丁分词词干加英语倾向后缀，前面还有表示分离的前缀 se-。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere 'to pick' with se- 'apart' gives seligere and selectus; -ivus supplies the English -ive that marks a tendency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legere「挑选」加 se-「分开」得 seligere 与 selectus；-ivus 提供英语 -ive，用以标记倾向。

items.meaning: given to choosing; narrow in effect
items.meaningCN: 惯于挑选的；作用范围窄的
items.example: The filter is selective for nitrate.

definition_zh: 安抚；平息；满足；姑息
definition_en: to calm someone's anger by giving in or making concessions
core_image: 递上一块糖，让哭闹的孩子安静下来
scene: 婴儿的哭声在车厢里回荡，母亲轻拍着他的背。 A bottle of warm milk appeased the crying baby.
sceneCN: 这里 appease 是「安抚」（第 1 个义项：用让步使怒气或不满平息）；句意为一瓶温奶安抚了哭闹的婴儿。

senses.title: To calm by giving in
senses.definition: to make someone less angry by agreeing to their demands or offering something
senses.definitionCN: 通过答应要求或给予东西使人息怒
senses.example: A bottle of warm milk appeased the crying baby.
senses.exampleCN: 一瓶温奶安抚了哭闹的婴儿。
senses.why: Pax means peace; the word pictures handing something over until peace returns.
senses.whyCN: pax 意为「和平」；这个词描绘的是交出些什么直到和平归来的画面。

senses.title: To satisfy a hunger or need
senses.definition: to relieve a strong desire or appetite by fulfilling it
senses.definitionCN: 通过满足来缓解强烈的欲望或需求
senses.example: A thick stew appeased their hunger after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 急行军后，一碗浓汤缓解了他们的饥饿。
senses.why: Hungry feelings behave like angry ones, so feeding and soothing share the verb.
senses.whyCN: 饥饿感的表现如同愤怒，于是「喂饱」与「抚慰」共用一个动词。

senses.title: To concede to an aggressor
senses.definition: to make political concessions to an aggressive power in hope of avoiding war
senses.definitionCN: 为避免战争而对侵略性政权作出政治让步
senses.example: The 1938 agreement is now remembered as appeasement.
senses.exampleCN: 1938 年的协定如今被记作绥靖的典型。
senses.why: Calming one aggressor scaled up from nursery to statecraft, with a bitter aftertaste.
senses.whyCN: 哄孩子的「安抚」放大为国家间的「绥靖」，且带上苦涩的贬义。

intro.en: Appease comes from Old French apaisier, from a- and pais 'peace', Latin pax.
intro.cn: appease 来自古法语 apaisier，由 a- 加 pais「和平」（拉丁语 pax）构成。

items.en: The root *peh₂k- meant 'to fasten', giving Latin pax, a binding agreement.
items.cn: 词根 *peh₂k- 意为「系结」，衍生出拉丁语 pax「缔结的和平」。

items.en: pax meant peace, originally a treaty bond.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，原指条约纽带。

items.cn: 古法语 apaisier 意为「使平息」。

items.en: Middle English adopted apesen in the thirteenth century.

items.en: After 1938 appeasement also carries the political charge of conceding to aggression.
items.cn: 1938 年之后，appeasement 亦带上了向侵略让步的政治贬义。
