definition_zh: 起诉；检控；（正式）继续从事、推行；追究到底
definition_en: to bring a criminal charge against someone and conduct the case
core_image: 一个人把一份文件按在桌上，沿着页边的编号一页页往下翻，翻到最后一页才停手
scene: 检方拿到新的银行记录之后，决定对那名会计正式提出指控。 The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecute 指对某人正式提起刑事指控并推进案件（第 1 个义项：提起刑事起诉）；句意：新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。图中可辨识物件：银行记录、案卷页码、检察官办公桌、印章。

pos.zh: 起诉；检控（对某人提起并推进刑事指控）
提起公诉；进行起诉
（正式）继续从事、推行（某项工作、调查或事业）

collocations.zh: 进行战争（旧式正式说法）

senses.title: Bring a criminal charge
senses.definition: to formally charge someone with an offence
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯罪
senses.example: The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind prosecution: what the office does when it decides a file should go to court.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 prosecution 背后的动作：当机构认定一份卷宗该送进法院时，它做的就是这件事。

senses.title: Conduct the case in court
senses.definition: to present and argue the state's case through the hearings
senses.definitionCN: 在庭审中陈述并论证国家的案件
senses.example: The office prosecuted the case for nearly two years.
senses.exampleCN: 该机关把这桩案子推进了近两年。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to follow forward, so the work is a long following of the case rather than a single filing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向前追随，所以这项工作是对案件的长程追随，而非一次立案。

senses.title: Press a civil claim
senses.definition: in legal writing, to pursue a claim or a suit to judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在法律文字中，把请求或诉讼追究至判决
senses.example: The creditor prosecuted the debt through two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人通过两级法院追究这笔债务。
senses.why: Before criminal law dominated the word, any claim could be prosecuted, and older legal writing still uses it that way.
senses.whyCN: 在刑法主导这个词之前，任何请求都可以被「追究」，较早的法律文字仍这样使用。

senses.title: Carry on an activity
senses.definition: in formal style, to continue or carry on a study, inquiry or policy
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，继续或推行一项研究、调查或政策
senses.example: The committee prosecuted its inquiry despite the delays.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管一再拖延，委员会仍把调查进行下去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is continuation, and formal prose keeps it alive for any sustained effort, not only for lawsuits.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「继续」，正式文字把它保留下来，用于任何持续的努力，而不限于诉讼。

senses.title: Pursue a war or campaign
senses.definition: in older usage, to carry a war or campaign forward energetically
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，有力地推进战争或战役
senses.example: The general prosecuted the campaign into the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 将军把战役推进到了冬季。
senses.why: Military writing used the verb for pressing an operation to its end, and that usage survives in histories and formal reports.
senses.whyCN: 军事文字用这个动词表示把一次行动压到终点，这一用法保存在史书与正式报告里。

senses.title: Carry out a duty or plan
senses.definition: in formal style, to carry out a duty, plan or design
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，执行一项职责、计划或设计
senses.example: She prosecuted the plan with a patience few colleagues shared.
senses.exampleCN: 她以少有人能及的耐心把这项计划执行下去。
senses.why: Any design can be followed through, and formal English uses the verb for that steady execution without any legal charge.
senses.whyCN: 任何设计都可以被贯彻到底，正式英语便用这个动词表示那种稳定的执行，与刑事指控无关。

senses.title: Follow up an appeal or remedy
senses.definition: to carry a legal remedy forward to the next stage
senses.definitionCN: 把一项法律救济推进到下一阶段
senses.example: They prosecuted the appeal all the way to the higher court.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把上诉一路推进到高等法院。
senses.why: A remedy has stages, and the verb marks the act of not letting the matter drop at the first refusal.
senses.whyCN: 救济是有阶段的，这个动词标记的正是「第一次被驳回也不放手」的那个动作。

senses.title: Pursue a goal relentlessly
senses.definition: in literary style, to pursue an aim with persistence
senses.definitionCN: 在文学文体中，坚持不懈地追求一个目标
senses.example: He prosecuted his ambition long after his friends had given up theirs.
senses.exampleCN: 朋友们早已放弃各自的抱负，他仍把自己的追求推进下去。
senses.why: The core image of following forward can describe any long pursuit, which is why the verb appears in writing about ambition.
senses.whyCN: 「向前追随」的核心意象可以描述任何长程追求，所以这个动词会出现在写抱负的文字里。

intro.en: Prosecute comes from the stem of Latin prosecutus, the past participle of prosequi 'to follow forward'. The verb was formed in English from that stem, and its oldest sense is continuation.
intro.cn: prosecute 来自拉丁 prosecutus 的词干，那是 prosequi「向前追随」的过去分词。这个动词是在英语中用该词干构成的，最古老的含义是「继续」。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it also stands behind sequence and consecutive, so the idea of one thing after another runs through the whole family.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，也是 sequence 与 consecutive 的来源，所以「一件接一件」的观念贯穿整族词。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, pursue, continue'. Roman legal writing used it for pursuing a charge.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。罗马法律文字用它表示追究一项指控。

items.en: The past participle prosecutus supplied the stem prosecut-, which English took as the base of both the verb and the nouns.
items.cn: 过去分词 prosecutus 提供词干 prosecut-，英语以它作为动词与名词的共同基础。

items.en: English formed prosecute from the participle stem, at first for continuing any business, then increasingly for the pursuit of a legal case.
items.cn: 英语用这个分词词干构成 prosecute，起初指继续任何事务，后来越来越多指追究一桩法律案件。

items.en: Legal writing fixed the criminal sense, pairing prosecute with indictment and trial, while the older sense of continuing survived in formal prose.
items.cn: 法律文字固定了刑事义，把 prosecute 与起诉、审判配对使用；而「继续」的旧义保存在正式散文中。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb mainly for criminal charges, with the sense of carrying out a duty, inquiry or war kept for formal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用这个动词指刑事指控；执行职责、进行调查或进行战争的义项则留给正式与历史文字。

note.en: Group one separates the related nouns from the classic hostile-prefix confusion and from a look-alike about looking forward; group two sets the verb against the other verbs of charging and suing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根名词、经典的「敌对前缀」混淆词，以及一个关于「向前看」的形近词；第二组把这个动词与其他表示指控和起诉的动词作对照。

entries.definition: To harass or oppress, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix replaces pursuit with mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指骚扰、压迫，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀把「追究」换成「迫害」。

entries.definition: The proceeding or the team; the verb names the act, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序或团队；动词命名的是动作，不是机构。

entries.definition: The lawyer who performs the act; the verb does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 执行这个动作的律师；动词本身不指人。

entries.definition: An outlook or a search for minerals, from prospicere 'to look forward'; it shares no following verb with prosecute.
entries.definitionCN: 指前景或找矿，来自 prospicere「向前看」；它与 prosecute 不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Capable of being prosecuted, a quality of a case rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被起诉的，是案件的性质，不是动作。

entries.definition: To charge formally, often after a grand jury; prosecute also covers the whole conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式起诉，常在大陪审团之后；prosecute 还覆盖案件的整个推进过程。

entries.definition: To state that someone has committed an offence; prosecute adds the decision and the conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指声明某人犯罪；prosecute 多了「决定起诉」与「推进案件」的意思。

entries.definition: To start a civil case; prosecute is the usual verb for criminal proceedings and can also mean carrying any claim forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起民事诉讼；prosecute 常用于刑事程序，也可指把任何请求推进下去。

entries.definition: To hear and decide a case in court; prosecute is the state's part before and during that hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法庭上审理并裁决；prosecute 是国家在庭审前后所做的那一部分。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for following an aim or a person; prosecute is its formal and legal doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 指追求目标或追踪某人的日常动词；prosecute 是它在正式与法律语境中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle stem and the real contrast between following a charge and harassing a person.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词词干，以及「追究指控」与「迫害他人」之间的真实对比。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: prosecuting a case means not letting it drop.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：起诉一桩案子就是不让它掉在地上。

normal.en: Persecute has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': it follows a person to hurt, not to court.
normal.cn: persecute 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀是「贯穿」：它跟住一个人是为了伤害，不是为了上法院。

normal.en: Prospect is about looking forward, not following: a different verb entirely.
normal.cn: prospect 讲的是向前看，不是跟随：完全另一个动词。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

normal.en: The old sense still works: a committee can prosecute an inquiry without charging anyone.
normal.cn: 旧义仍然可用：委员会可以把一项调查进行下去，而不指控任何人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger walking down a numbered page, page after page, until the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着编号的页面往下走，一页又一页，直到最后一页。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a heavy door that must be pushed open again at every stage.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一扇沉重的门，每到一个阶段都得再推一次。

abstract.en: Picture a person who keeps pursuing a goal after everyone else has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都停下之后，仍有一个人在追求那个目标。

examples.en: The state may prosecute only if the evidence meets a fixed standard.
examples.cn: 只有证据达到固定标准，州一方才可以起诉。

examples.en: They prosecuted him for fraud and lost the first hearing.
examples.cn: 他们以欺诈罪起诉他，却输掉了第一次庭审。

examples.en: The council prosecuted the inquiry for three years.
examples.cn: 委员会把这项调查进行了三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究」——把诉状剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的过去分词 prosecutus 的词干 prosecut-；由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from bringing a criminal charge, through conducting the case, pursuing a civil claim, carrying on an inquiry, pressing a war, executing a plan, following up an appeal, and pursuing a goal in literary style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从提起刑事指控开始，经推进案件、追究民事请求、进行调查、推进战争、执行计划、追究上诉，最后到文学文体中的执着追求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger walking down a numbered page to the last line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着编号的页面走到最后一行。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: the act starts a criminal case and then keeps it moving.
branches.cn: 指控：这个动作启动刑事案件，然后又不断把它往前推。

branches.en: THE CIVIL CLAIM: the same verb reaches claims that are not criminal at all.
branches.cn: 民事请求：同一个动词也覆盖完全不属于刑事的请求。

branches.en: THE FORMAL EFFORT: any inquiry, duty or plan can be carried forward.
branches.cn: 正式的努力：任何调查、职责或计划都可以被推行。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: wars and appeals are both pressed on to their next stage.
branches.cn: 推进：战争与上诉都被压向下一阶段。

branches.en: THE LITERARY EDGE: the same following motion becomes a picture of relentless ambition.
branches.cn: 文学边缘：同一个「追随」动作成了不知停歇的抱负图景。

intro.en: Prosecute is a verb built on a Latin participle stem, and its endings are what turn that stem into an English action word.
intro.cn: prosecute 是建立在拉丁分词词干上的动词，词尾把那个词干变成英语的动作词。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth', sequi 'follow' and the participle stem prosecut- are the pieces; English added the verb ending -e to make prosecute.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是 pro-「向前」、sequi「跟随」与分词词干 prosecut-；英语加上动词词尾 -e 构成 prosecute。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀把跟随指向前方）
已追究的（提供英语词干 prosecut-）
追究一项指控（由词干加动词词尾，成为可变化的英语动词）
对案件的追究（名词后缀把动作转成程序）
追究指控的人（施事后缀把动作转成施事者）
可被起诉的（形容词后缀把动作转成可能性）

definition_zh: 地质年代；地层或岩石的年龄；地质时代的划分单位
definition_en: the age of a rock, fossil or event measured in geological time, or a named division of earth history
core_image: 剖面图上一条条界线，把厚厚的地层分成不同的年代
scene: 学生在剖面图上标出各层的界线，老师提醒他们先确定每一层的年代再谈化石。 Each bed was assigned a geological age before any fossil was identified.
sceneCN: 这里 geological age 指「某一地层的年代」（第 3 个义项：地层形成的地质年代）；句意为在鉴定任何化石之前，先给每一层定出地质年代。图中可辨识物件：剖面图、层界线条、铅笔标记、化石符号。

pos.zh: 地质年代；地质年龄；地质时代的划分（可数复合名词）

senses.title: A division of earth history
senses.titleCN: 地球历史的一个划分单位
senses.definition: a named interval of geological time, such as a period or an epoch, used to place events in order
senses.definitionCN: 有名称的地质时间间隔，如纪或世，用于把事件排序
senses.example: The Cambrian is the geological age in which hard shells first became common.
senses.exampleCN: 寒武纪是硬壳首次普遍出现的地质年代。
senses.why: the phrase can name an interval rather than a measurement, which is why it appears in tables of periods and epochs.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以命名一段时间而非一个测量值，因此出现在纪与世的表格中。

senses.title: The absolute age of a rock
senses.definition: the age of a rock or mineral in years, obtained by radiometric dating
senses.definitionCN: 通过放射性定年得到的岩石或矿物年龄，以年计
senses.example: The geological age of the granite came out at three hundred million years.
senses.exampleCN: 这块花岗岩的地质年龄测出来是三亿年。
senses.why: the phrase shifts from a named interval to a number, and the method, not the name, does the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从命名的时段转到数字，起决定作用的是方法而非名称。

senses.title: The age of a bed
senses.definition: the time at which a particular layer was deposited
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定层沉积形成的时期
senses.example: Each bed was assigned a geological age before any fossil was identified.
senses.exampleCN: 在鉴定任何化石之前，先给每一层定出地质年代。
senses.why: stratigraphy speaks of the age of a bed rather than of a sample, because the layer is the unit that can be mapped.
senses.whyCN: 地层学说的是层的年代而非样品的年代，因为层才是可填图的单位。

senses.title: A named era or period
senses.definition: one of the formal divisions of the geological timescale, from eon down to stage
senses.definitionCN: 地质年代表中的正式划分之一，从宙到阶
senses.example: The age of reptiles ended with the extinction at the boundary.
senses.exampleCN: 爬行动物的时代以界线处的那次灭绝告终。
senses.why: popular writing uses age for the great divisions, while formal stratigraphy prefers period, epoch and stage.
senses.whyCN: 通俗写作把这个词用于大划分，正式地层学则偏好 period、epoch 与 stage。

senses.title: The age indicated by a fossil
senses.definition: the time range that a fossil species implies for the rock in which it is found
senses.definitionCN: 某一化石物种为其所在岩层指示的时间范围
senses.example: The ammonite gives the bed a geological age no younger than the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 这件菊石给该层一个不晚于侏罗纪的地质年代。
senses.why: biostratigraphy converts a fossil into a date, so the phrase often appears where index species are discussed.
senses.whyCN: 生物地层学把化石换算成年代，因此这个短语常出现在讨论标志物种之处。

senses.title: The age of the Earth
senses.definition: the elapsed time since the formation of the Earth, now measured at about four and a half billion years
senses.definitionCN: 自地球形成以来经过的时间，现测约四十五亿年
senses.example: Attempts to fix the geological age of the Earth ended the argument over a young planet.
senses.exampleCN: 测定地球地质年龄的尝试终结了年轻地球之争。
senses.why: the singular phrase became a famous scientific question, and its answer changed the standing of geology.
senses.whyCN: 这个单数短语成了一个著名的科学问题，其答案改变了地质学的地位。

senses.title: The geological setting of a find
senses.titleCN: 发现物的地质年代背景
senses.definition: the geological period and conditions in which an archaeological or palaeontological find is set
senses.definitionCN: 考古或古生物发现所处的时期与地质条件
senses.example: The tools lay in deposits of the same geological age as the cave fill.
senses.exampleCN: 这些工具所在的堆积与洞穴填充物属于同一地质年代。
senses.why: cross-disciplinary work needs the phrase because a find's date may rest on the enclosing sediment rather than on the object.
senses.whyCN: 跨学科工作需要这个短语，因为发现物的年代可能取决于围岩，而非物件本身。

senses.title: An impossibly long span, in speech
senses.definition: used exaggeration for a wait or a period that feels endless
senses.definitionCN: 夸张地指漫长得仿佛无尽的等待或时期
senses.example: It took a geological age for the bus to arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 等公交车仿佛等了一个地质年代。
senses.why: the joke works because geological ages are measured in millions of years, so any delay becomes absurdly small beside them.
senses.whyCN: 这个玩笑之所以成立，是因为地质年代以百万年计，任何等待相比之下都小得可笑。

intro.en: Geological age joins geology, from Greek gē 'earth' and -logia 'study', to age, from Latin aetas through Old French aage. The phrase settled as a technical term in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geological age 由 geology（希腊 gē「大地」+ -logia「研究」）与 age（拉丁 aetas 经古法语 aage）组合而成。这个短语在十九世纪固定为技术术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gē meant 'earth, land'; it opens geology, geography and geometry, each with a different second element.
items.cn: gē 意为「大地、土地」；它开启 geology、geography 与 geometry，各自第二个成分不同。

items.en: -logia 'study, account' comes from logos; geology was coined in the eighteenth century for the study of the earth's structure.
items.cn: -logia「研究、论述」来自 logos；geology 于十八世纪造出，指对地球构造的研究。

items.en: Aetas meant 'lifetime, age, period'; through Old French aage it became English age, covering both a person's years and a historical span.
items.cn: aetas 意为「寿命、年龄、时期」；经古法语 aage 成为英语 age，兼指人的年岁与历史时段。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists combined the two to speak of the age of a bed, a fossil or the earth, and the phrase became standard.
items.cn: 十九世纪地质学家把两者组合，用来谈层、化石或地球的年龄，这个短语遂成标准。

items.en: As the geological timescale was formalized, age also came to name the great divisions themselves.
items.cn: 随着地质年代表被正式化，age 也开始指那些大划分本身。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dating only): both elements are secure, but the phrase's earliest fixed use varies by author and by sense.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：两个成分都确定，但该短语最早固定使用的年代因作者与义项而异。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its near compounds and adjective forms; group two separates it from words for time divisions and measurements.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与近义复合形式及形容词分开；第二组区分它与时间划分、测量的其它说法。

entries.definition: The same sense written with the shorter adjective; both are current, and geologic is commoner in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意义用较短形容词表达；两者通行，geologic 在美式用法中更常见。

entries.definition: The complete framework of eras, periods and epochs; a single age is one slot within it.
entries.definitionCN: 由代、纪、世构成的完整框架；单个 age 是其中一格。

entries.definition: The branch that measures rock ages by radiometric methods; the phrase names the result, not the method.
entries.definitionCN: 用放射性方法测定岩石年龄的学科；短语指结果，而非方法。

entries.definition: An era is one of the largest divisions, containing several periods; an age may be much shorter.
entries.definitionCN: 代是最大的划分之一，含若干纪；age 可能短得多。

entries.definition: A formal subdivision of an era in the timescale, such as the Jurassic; it is more precise than the loose word age.
entries.definitionCN: 年代表中代的正式细分，如侏罗纪；比松散的 age 更精确。

entries.definition: A subdivision of a period, such as the Pleistocene; it is shorter than most ages in popular use.
entries.definitionCN: 纪的细分，如更新世；比通俗用法中的多数 age 更短。

entries.definition: A specific point in time or a measured number of years; age can mean either a span or a measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体时点或测得的年数；age 可指时段，也可指测量值。

entries.definition: A long span with a characteristic character, geological or historical; it is vaguer than a formal period.
entries.definitionCN: 具有代表性特征的漫长时间，地质或历史皆可；比正式纪更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: geology 'earth study' + age 'lifetime, span': the span of earth time assigned to a rock.
normal.cn: geology「大地研究」+ age「寿命、时段」：分配给某块岩石的地球时间跨度。

normal.en: The family runs geology, geologic, geologist, geochronology, geological timescale.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 geology、geologic、geologist、geochronology、geological timescale。

normal.en: Two readings: a named division, or a number of years.
normal.cn: 两种读法：一个有名称的划分，或一个年数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: relative geological age, absolute geological age, age of the Earth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：相对地质年代、绝对地质年龄、地球的年龄。

normal.en: The everyday joke works because the unit is millions of years.
normal.cn: 日常玩笑成立，是因为这个单位以百万年计。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid along a cliff, with each bed given a number.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子沿崖壁铺开，每层都标上一个数。

abstract.en: Picture a library where each shelf is a million years and the book you want is on one of them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每层书架是一百万年，你要的书在其一。

abstract.en: Picture a queue so slow that the wait is measured in stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条慢到用石头计时的队伍。

examples.en: The geological age of the lava flow was fixed by radiometric dating.
examples.cn: 这次熔岩流的地质年龄由放射性定年确定。

examples.en: Fossils of the same geological age occur on three continents.
examples.cn: 同一地质年代的化石出现在三个大洲。

examples.en: It took a geological age to get a reply from the ministry.
examples.cn: 从部里得到答复仿佛等了一个地质年代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「geo（大地）+ logical（学问的）+ age（年代）」——研究大地所得出的年代 → 地质年代

root: geology（希腊 gē「大地」+ -logia「研究」）+ age（拉丁 aetas「寿命、时期」经古法语 aage）；十九世纪固定为技术短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a named division to a measured number, then to a single bed, a fossil, the whole planet, a find's setting and a joke about waiting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从有名称的划分走到测量数值，再到单一层、化石、整个行星、发现物的背景，以及关于等待的玩笑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid along a cliff, each bed given its own number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子沿崖壁铺开，每一层都有自己的数字。

branches.en: NAMED TIME: formal divisions and popular eras are the same scale read at different precision.
branches.cn: 命名的时间：正式划分与通俗时代，是同一尺度以不同精度读取。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: a rock's years and a bed's date differ in object, not in method.
branches.cn: 测量：岩石的年数与层的年代，对象不同而方法相同。

branches.en: FOSSIL AS CLOCK: an index species converts stone into a date.
branches.cn: 化石作钟：标志物种把石头换算成年代。

branches.en: WHOLE PLANET AND LOCAL SETTING: the same phrase scales from the earth to a find.
branches.cn: 整个行星与局部背景：同一短语从地球缩到一件发现物。

branches.en: HYPERBOLE: a unit of millions makes any wait laughably short.
branches.cn: 夸张：以百万年为单位，任何等待都短得可笑。

intro.en: Geological age is a two-word technical phrase whose parts come from Greek and Latin respectively, and each part still builds families.
intro.cn: geological age 是两词技术短语，两部分分别来自希腊语与拉丁语，且各自仍在构词。

latinIntro.en: Greek gē 'earth' plus -logia 'study' gives geology; Latin aetas 'lifetime' gives age through French. Latin entries record aetas and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 gē「大地」加 -logia「研究」给出 geology；拉丁 aetas「寿命」经法语给出 age。latinEntries 记录 aetas 及其同族。

items.example: The prefix fixes the planet as the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把行星固定为对象。
地质学与生物学共用它。

items.meaning: of the study of the earth

items.structure: aetas (Latin 'lifetime, period') via Old French aage
items.example: Age can mean a person's years or an era.
items.exampleCN: age 可指人的年岁，也可指一个时代。

items.meaning: the date of a rock or a division of time
items.example: Each bed has its own geological age.
items.exampleCN: 每层都有自己的地质年代。

items.example: Geology grew from mining and mapping.
items.exampleCN: 地质学从采矿与测绘发展而来。
地质年代学给熔岩流定年。
年代表给所有年代排序。

definition_zh: 亵渎；辱骂神明；冒犯神圣之物
definition_en: to speak about God or sacred things with disrespect
core_image: 对着神像吐口水的人
scene: 暴徒闯入圣殿，守门人惊恐地退后。 They were punished for blaspheming against the gods.
sceneCN: 这里 blaspheme 是「亵渎神明」（第 1 个义项：以言行辱没神圣）；句意是他们因亵渎众神而受到惩罚。

pos.zh: 亵渎；辱骂（神明）
口出渎神之言

derivatives.zh: blaspheme 加 -y，义为「渎神行为；渎神言辞」
blaspheme 加 -ous，义为「亵渎神明的」

senses.title: To speak against God or gods
senses.definition: to show disrespect for God or sacred beings in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以言语不敬上帝或神圣存在
senses.example: They were punished for blaspheming against the gods.
senses.exampleCN: 他们因亵渎众神而受到惩罚。
senses.why: Greek blasphemein meant to speak evil, and speech against the divine is its gravest case.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 blasphemein 意为「出言诋毁」，指向神明的恶言是其最重者。

senses.title: To treat sacred things with contempt
senses.definition: to show contempt for holy places, books, or symbols
senses.definitionCN: 以轻蔑态度对待圣地、圣书或圣物
senses.example: Vandals blasphemed the shrine with graffiti.
senses.exampleCN: 破坏者用涂鸦亵渎了圣坛。
senses.why: What speech does to God, action does to His symbols.
senses.whyCN: 言语如何冒犯神，行为便如何冒犯神的象征。

senses.title: To curse and swear irreverently
senses.definition: to use God's name in curses and swearing
senses.definitionCN: 在咒骂中滥用神之名
senses.example: Sailors blaspheming in the storm were sternly rebuked.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴中以神名咒骂的水手受到了严厉训斥。
senses.why: A holy name spent on anger cheapens it, which is the root offence.
senses.whyCN: 把圣名挥霍在怒气上便贬损了它，这正是冒犯的根本。

senses.title: To revile what others hold sacred
senses.definition: to attack beliefs or figures another group reveres
senses.definitionCN: 攻击其他群体所尊崇的信仰或人物
senses.example: Critics accused him of blaspheming national heroes.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指责他亵渎民族英雄。
senses.why: The word stretches from gods to anything treated as untouchable.
senses.whyCN: 该词由神明延展至一切被视为不可触碰之物。

senses.title: To violate deeply held values
senses.definition: to act against principles treated as sacred in a society
senses.definitionCN: 以行为触犯社会视为神圣的原则
senses.example: To them, waste blasphemed against the gospel of thrift.
senses.exampleCN: 在他们看来，浪费亵渎了节俭的信条。
senses.why: Secular creeds inherit the old severity toward their own taboos.
senses.whyCN: 世俗信条承袭了旧日对自身禁忌的严厉。

senses.title: To deny or mock doctrine
senses.definition: to reject or ridicule accepted religious teaching
senses.definitionCN: 否认或讥讽公认的宗教教义
senses.example: He was tried for blaspheming church doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 他因嘲弄教会教义而受审。
senses.why: Doctrine is speech made sacred; mocking it is speech against speech.
senses.whyCN: 教义是被神圣化的言说，嘲弄它便是以言攻言。

senses.title: To speak impiously of nature or art
senses.definition: to treat nature's power or great art with jarring disrespect
senses.definitionCN: 以刺目的轻慢态度对待自然伟力或伟大艺术
senses.example: Building a car park there seemed to blaspheme the landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 在那里建停车场似乎亵渎了这片风景。
senses.why: Reverence transfers from altars to mountains and masterpieces.
senses.whyCN: 敬畏之心自祭坛延伸至山川与杰作。

senses.title: To profane an oath or promise
senses.definition: to break or cheapen what was sworn before God
senses.definitionCN: 背弃或在神前立下的誓约
senses.example: Perjury blasphemes the very court's sacred forms.
senses.exampleCN: 伪证亵渎了法庭庄严的形式。
senses.why: An oath borrows God as witness; betraying it insults the witness.
senses.whyCN: 誓言以神为见证，背誓便是羞辱见证者。

intro.en: Blaspheme comes from Greek blasphemein, to speak evil of.
intro.cn: blaspheme 来自希腊语 blasphemein「出言诋毁」。

items.en: possibly from roots meaning harmful plus fame or speech; the compound's parts are debated.
items.cn: 一般认为由「伤害」与「名声／言语」两词根复合，构词细节有争议。

items.en: blasphemein meant to speak ill, slander, later specifically revile the gods.
items.cn: 希腊语 blasphemein 意为「说坏话、诽谤」，后专指辱骂神明。

items.en: blasphemare carried the religious sense into church Latin.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 blasphemare 将宗教义带入教会拉丁语。

items.en: blasphemer kept the sense of reviling God.
items.cn: 古法语 blasphemer 保留「辱骂上帝」之义。

items.en: English took the word through French for both cursing and offending the sacred.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪经法语借入，兼指咒骂与冒犯神圣。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blasph- root; the near-meaning group gathers words of religious offence.
note.cn: 形近组共享 blasph- 词根；近义组汇集宗教冒犯类词。

definition_zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；（军事）突破防线
definition_en: a sudden important advance that gets past a barrier, especially in science, medicine, technology, or the military
core_image: 一堵墙上被撞开的第一道缺口，后面的人由此穿过去
scene: 实验室熬夜三个月后，第一块样品终于通过了测试。 On the lab screen the long-unsolved structure finally resolved, and the team leader said, This is the breakthrough we needed.
sceneCN: 这里 breakthrough 是「重大突破、突破性进展」（第 2 个义项：科研上越过长期障碍）；句意：实验室屏幕上多年无解的结构终于显出清晰轮廓，团队负责人说，这就是他们需要的突破。场景要点：屏幕上的结构图、实验台、团队、记录板。

pos.zh: 突破；重大进展；突破性成果；军事突破

derivatives.zh: 爆发痛（慢性疼痛治疗中突然发作的剧痛）
突破性感染（接种或服药后仍发生的感染）
突破性技术（名词作定语）

senses.title: Military: a hole forced in a defensive line
senses.titleCN: 军事：在防线中强行打开缺口
senses.definition: a successful advance through an enemy's defensive line, opening a gap for the rest of the force
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过敌方防线，为其余部队打开缺口
senses.example: The armoured division made a breakthrough at dawn and pushed into open ground.
senses.exampleCN: 装甲师在黎明时突破防线，向开阔地推进。
senses.why: Breakthrough began as a noun from the phrase break through: a line is broken and the force passes through the hole. The earliest recorded modern noun use is military, from the trench warfare of the late 1910s.
senses.whyCN: breakthrough 最初是短语 break through 名词化的结果：防线被打破，部队从缺口穿过去。最早有记录的现代名词用法是军事义，来自 1910 年代后期的堑壕战。

senses.title: Science and technology: an advance past a long barrier
senses.titleCN: 科研与技术：越过长期障碍的进展
senses.definition: a sudden, important advance that solves a problem or removes an obstacle that had blocked work for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而重要的进展，解决了一个问题或清除了长期阻碍工作的障碍
senses.example: The team's breakthrough came when they could finally image the protein's active site.
senses.exampleCN: 当团队终于能成像该蛋白的活性位点时，他们的突破到来了。
senses.why: The military gap becomes an intellectual gap. Something long closed is suddenly open, and work that was stuck can move forward; this transfer is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack.
senses.whyCN: 军事上的缺口变成了知识上的缺口。长期封闭的东西突然打开，卡住的工作得以推进；这一转移自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。

senses.title: Medicine: a treatment that changes the outcome
senses.definition: a new drug, test, or procedure that greatly improves the treatment of a disease
senses.definitionCN: 极大改善某种疾病治疗的新药、检测或疗法
senses.example: The drug was hailed as a breakthrough for patients who had run out of options.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药被赞为那些已无其他选择的患者的突破。
senses.why: The barrier here is disease or a failed treatment, and the advance passes through it. Medical writing adopts the word because it captures both the obstacle and the sudden release, keeping the battlefield shape intact.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍是疾病或失效的疗法，而进展穿过了它。医学写作采用这个词，因为它同时抓住障碍与突然的解除，并保持战场的形状不变。

senses.title: Personal: breaking a deadlock or limit
senses.definition: a moment when a person gets past a mental block, a deadlock, or a limit that had held them back
senses.definitionCN: 一个人越过心理障碍、僵局或长期限制自己的极限的时刻
senses.example: Learning to speak in public was a personal breakthrough for him.
senses.exampleCN: 学会公开演讲对他而言是一次个人突破。
senses.why: The wall is now inside the person: fear, habit, or a fixed limit. The same shape holds — a barrier is met and passed — which is why the word feels natural outside science and warfare.
senses.whyCN: 墙现在在人的内心：恐惧、习惯或固定极限。形状不变——遇到障碍并越过去——因此这个词用在科学与战争之外也很自然。

senses.title: Business and market: opening a closed door
senses.titleCN: 商业与市场：打开一扇关着的门
senses.definition: a product, deal, or strategy that lets a company enter a new market or reach a new level
senses.definitionCN: 让公司进入新市场或达到新水平的产品、交易或策略
senses.example: The low-cost model was the company's breakthrough into emerging markets.
senses.exampleCN: 低成本模式是这家公司进入新兴市场的突破。
senses.why: A closed market is treated as a wall, and a successful entry as the hole through it. Business English borrows the military image and keeps its force, so entering a market becomes a passage through a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 封闭的市场被当作一堵墙，成功进入就是墙上打开的洞。商业英语借用了军事意象并保留其力度，于是进入市场变成了穿过障碍。

senses.title: Attributive use: breakthrough drug, technology, year
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：突破性药物、技术、年份
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark the thing as the one that produced the advance, as in breakthrough technology
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，标记该事物就是产生突破的那一个，如 breakthrough technology
senses.example: The breakthrough technology cut the cost of sequencing by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。
senses.why: The noun is placed before another noun without a suffix, a zero-derived modifier. It names not a general quality but the specific advance that opened the way, so the modifier keeps the concrete event.
senses.whyCN: 名词不加后缀直接放在另一个名词前，构成零派生修饰语。它命名的不是一般性质，而是打开道路的那次具体突破，因此修饰语保留具体事件。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus discovery
senses.definition: a discovery is something found; a breakthrough is a discovery or advance that passes a barrier and changes what can be done next
senses.definitionCN: discovery 是被发现的东西；breakthrough 是越过障碍、改变接下来能做之事的新发现或进展
senses.example: The discovery of the fossil was interesting, but the dating method was the breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 发现化石本身很有意思，但真正突破的是测年方法。
senses.why: Discovery names the find; breakthrough adds the wall and the passage. A discovery can be small and still be a discovery, but a breakthrough must change the situation, because the break is part of its meaning.
senses.whyCN: discovery 命名“找到的东西”；breakthrough 额外包含“墙”与“穿过”。发现可以很小仍是发现，而突破必须改变局面，因为“打破”是它意义的一部分。

senses.title: Usage boundary: breakthrough versus advance and progress
senses.definition: advance and progress can be gradual; breakthrough implies a sudden, decisive jump past an obstacle
senses.definitionCN: advance 与 progress 可以是渐进的；breakthrough 暗示突然而决定性地越过障碍
senses.example: Years of steady progress led to one breakthrough.
senses.exampleCN: 多年稳步进展最终带来一次突破。
senses.why: The compound contains break, a sudden verb, so it cannot describe slow improvement. This is why journalists reserve it for the moment the wall gives way, while progress can continue for years.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组含有 break 这个表示突然动作的动词，因此不能描述缓慢改善。这也是记者只把它留给墙崩塌那一刻的原因，而 progress 可以持续多年。

senses.title: Specialized: breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain
senses.titleCN: 专业用法：突破性感染与爆发痛
senses.definition: in medical compounds, breakthrough describes something that gets past a defence, such as a vaccine or a painkiller
senses.definitionCN: 在医学复合词中，breakthrough 描述越过某种防御的东西，如疫苗或止痛药
senses.example: A breakthrough infection occurred in a few vaccinated patients.
senses.exampleCN: 少数已接种患者发生了突破性感染。
senses.why: These compounds use the oldest literal sense: the pathogen or the pain breaks through the defence that was supposed to hold it. The barrier is medical, but the image is unchanged, so the noun keeps its military geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这些复合词用的是最古老的字面义：病原体或疼痛突破了本应拦住它的防线。障碍是医学的，但意象没有变，因此名词保留了军事几何。

intro.en: Breakthrough is not a Latin derivative. It is the English phrase break through turned into a noun: two native Old English words, a verb of breaking and a word of passing through, welded into one compound. Etymonline dates the noun to 1918 in a military sense; the exact first occurrence is uncertain.
intro.cn: breakthrough 不是拉丁派生词。它是英语短语 break through 名词化的结果：两个本土古英语词——表示“打破”的动词与表示“穿过”的词——焊合为一个复合词。etymonline 把名词的军事义定在 1918 年；确切的最早出现存疑。

items.en: Break goes back to Old English brecan 'to divide solid matter violently, to burst, to break', from Proto-Germanic *brekanan and PIE root *bhreg- 'to break'. Through goes back to Old English þurh, from Proto-Germanic *thurx and PIE *tere- 'to cross over, pass through, overcome'. Neither word is Latin or Greek.
items.cn: break 上溯古英语 brecan“猛烈分开固体、爆裂、打破”，来自原始日耳曼语 *brekanan 与原始印欧语词根 *bhreg-“打破”。through 上溯古英语 þurh，来自原始日耳曼语 *thurx 与原始印欧语 *tere-“越过、穿过、克服”。两者都不是拉丁语或希腊语。

items.en: The verbal phrase break through is attested from about 1400 in the sense 'overcome or penetrate a barrier'. The verb keeps its sudden force, and the later noun inherits that suddenness.
items.cn: 短语动词 break through 约自 1400 年起有记录，意为“克服或穿透障碍”。动词保留突然的力度，后来的名词继承了这种突然性。

items.en: Etymonline records the noun breakthrough (also written break-through) from 1918, meaning a 'significant or sudden advance', in a military sense. The date fits the trench warfare of the First World War, but the exact first written occurrence is uncertain and may be slightly earlier.
items.cn: etymonline 记录名词 breakthrough（也写作 break-through）自 1918 年起表示军事上的“重大或突然的推进”。这个年代与第一次世界大战的堑壕战相符，但确切的最早书面出现存疑，可能略早。

items.en: The meaning 'abrupt solution or progress' is recorded from the 1930s, on the notion of a successful attack. The wall becomes a research problem, a disease, or a personal limit, and the passage through it becomes a decisive advance.
items.cn: “突然的解决或进展”义自 1930 年代有记录，依托的是“进攻成功”的意象。墙变成研究难题、疾病或个人极限，而穿过墙的通道变成决定性的进展。

items.en: Medicine applied the word to drugs and procedures that change outcomes, and business to products that open new markets. The attributive use, as in breakthrough technology, is a zero-derived modifier with no suffix.
items.cn: 医学把这个词用于改变结局的药物与疗法，商业把它用于打开新市场的产品。breakthrough technology 这类定语用法是零派生修饰语，不加后缀。

items.en: Journalism has inflated the word, so it is often used for any good news. Technical compounds such as breakthrough infection and breakthrough pain keep the strict literal sense of something passing a defence. The noun remains a native English compound, not a borrowed root.
items.cn: 新闻写作把这个词用滥了，常用来指任何好消息。breakthrough infection、breakthrough pain 等技术复合词则保留“某物越过防御”的严格字面义。这个名词始终是本土英语复合词，而不是借来的词根。

note.en: The first group is the same break + particle pattern with different particles and different results; the second separates a breakthrough from a find, a gradual gain, a jump, and a new method.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 break + 小品词的构词模式，但小品词与结果不同；第二组把突破与发现、渐进增益、跃升及新方法区分开。

entries.definition: The end of a relationship or the splitting of a group. Up here means apart, so the compound is about separation, not passage.
entries.definitionCN: 关系结束或团体分裂。这里的 up 表示“分开”，因此复合词说的是分离，而不是穿过。

entries.definition: An escape from a place or a sudden success that escapes a limited category. Out stresses leaving a container, not crossing a line.
entries.definitionCN: 从某处逃出，或突然脱离某一局限类别的成功。out 强调离开容器，而不是越过一条线。

entries.definition: A failure of a machine, system, or person, or an analysis into parts. Down marks collapse or division, the opposite direction from through.
entries.definitionCN: 机器、系统或人的崩溃，或分解为部分。down 标记崩塌或分解，与 through 的方向相反。

entries.definition: A separation or departure from a group, as in a breakaway faction. Away marks distance from the source, not a passage to the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 从群体中分离或脱离，如 breakaway faction。away 标记远离源头，而不是穿到另一边。

entries.definition: The act of finding something that was already there but unknown. It names the find, while breakthrough names the barrier passed.
entries.definitionCN: 发现原本存在却未知之物的行为。它命名“找到”，而 breakthrough 命名“越过的障碍”。

entries.definition: A forward movement or improvement, often gradual. It lacks the sudden break that breakthrough requires.
entries.definitionCN: 向前的移动或改善，常为渐进。它没有 breakthrough 所要求的突然断裂。

entries.definition: A very large and sudden change, as in a leap in technology. It stresses distance jumped rather than a wall broken.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而突然的变化，如技术上的 leap。它强调跳过的距离，而不是打破一堵墙。

entries.definition: A new idea, method, or product actually put into use. It stresses novelty and application, not the overcoming of an obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 被实际采用的新想法、方法或产品。它强调新颖与应用，而不是克服障碍。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: break + through, the military gap, and real medical compounds such as breakthrough infection.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：break + through 的构词、军事缺口，以及 breakthrough infection 等真实医学复合词。

normal.en: break + through: first a wall is broken, then people pass through the hole. The noun keeps both halves of that action.
normal.cn: break + through：先打破一堵墙，再有人从洞里穿过去。名词同时保留这一动作的两半。

normal.en: The word grew in the trenches: a breakthrough was a hole in the enemy line, not a clever idea.
normal.cn: 这个词在堑壕里长大：breakthrough 是敌军防线上的一个缺口，而不是一个聪明点子。

normal.en: When a lab says breakthrough, it borrows the trench image: the problem was a wall, and now there is a way through.
normal.cn: 实验室说 breakthrough 时借用了堑壕的意象：问题是一堵墙，现在有路可过了。

normal.en: breakthrough technology is the technology that made the hole; the modifier names the specific advance, not a general quality.
normal.cn: breakthrough technology 就是打出缺口的那个技术；修饰语命名的是具体那次突破，不是一般性质。

normal.en: breakthrough infection is literal: the germ breaks through the vaccine's defence. The old image survives in the clinic.
normal.cn: breakthrough infection 是字面义：病原体突破了疫苗的防线。旧意象在诊室里活了下来。

abstract.en: A wall is not removed; a hole is made. A breakthrough does not erase the obstacle, it creates a passage through it.
abstract.cn: 墙没有被移走，只是被打开一个洞。突破并不消除障碍，而是在障碍上开出一条通路。

abstract.en: Before the break, every step is blocked; after it, the same energy moves freely. The word marks the single instant when the direction changes.
abstract.cn: 在断裂之前，每一步都被挡住；之后，同样的力气自由流动。这个词标记方向改变的那一瞬。

abstract.en: A breakthrough is a door that was not there yesterday: the room behind it was always there, but no one could enter.
abstract.cn: 突破是昨天还不存在的一扇门：门后的房间一直都在，只是没人进得去。

examples.en: The vaccine was the first real breakthrough in the fight against the disease.
examples.cn: 这种疫苗是对抗该疾病的第一项真正突破。

examples.en: Years of failed experiments made the final breakthrough feel sudden.
examples.cn: 多年失败的实验让最后的突破显得很突然。

examples.en: The company's breakthrough into the Japanese market came through a local partner.
examples.cn: 这家公司借本地伙伴实现了进入日本市场的突破。

dict_mnemonic.text: “布雷克思如”——先把墙 break（打破），再 through（穿过去）→ breakthrough 突破

root: 英语本土短语 break through 的名词化；break 来自古英语 brecan“打破”，through 来自古英语 þurh“穿过”。不是拉丁派生，而是“动词 + 方位小品词”的复合。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of breakthrough share one shape: a barrier is broken and something passes through it. The barrier may be a trench line, a research problem, a disease, a personal limit, a closed market, or a vaccine defence.
sensesIntro.cn: breakthrough 的九个义项形状相同：障碍被打破，某物穿过去。障碍可以是战壕防线、研究难题、疾病、个人极限、封闭市场，或疫苗防线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall is broken at one point, and what was blocked can now pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙在某一点被打破，原本被挡住的东西现在可以通过。

branches.en: BATTLE: the literal gap in a defensive line, the historical seed of the word.
branches.cn: 战场：防线上字面的缺口，这个词的历史种子。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE AND CURE: a research problem or a disease becomes the wall that is passed.
branches.cn: 知识与治疗：研究难题或疾病变成被越过的墙。

branches.en: SELF: the barrier moves inside a person, as fear or a fixed limit.
branches.cn: 自我：障碍移到人的内心，成为恐惧或固定极限。

branches.en: MARKET AND MODIFIER: a closed market is a wall, and the breakthrough product is the thing that made the hole.
branches.cn: 市场与定语：封闭市场是一堵墙，而突破性产品就是打出缺口的那个东西。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: discovery names the find, advance names a gradual step, and medical compounds keep the literal defence.
branches.cn: 边界：discovery 命名发现，advance 命名渐进一步，医学复合词则保留字面的防御义。

intro.en: Breakthrough has no affixes at all. It is a compound of break and through, both native English words; the noun is a zero-derivation from the phrasal verb, with no suffix added.
intro.cn: breakthrough 没有任何词缀。它是 break 与 through 两个本土英语词的复合；名词由短语动词零派生而来，没有添加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer here. The word is native English, so the Latin entries below are not ancestors but Latin-derived counterparts that English already had for a forward step or a find.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语层次。这个词是本土英语，因此下面的拉丁条目不是祖先，而是英语中原本就有的、表示“向前一步”或“发现”的拉丁来源对应词。

items.structure: break (to break) + through (from one side to the other)
items.meaning: to force a way through an obstacle; the source phrase, later compressed into a noun
items.meaningCN: 强行穿过障碍；这是源短语，后来压缩成名词
items.example: The water broke through the dam at midnight.

items.meaning: the gap and the passage through it; no suffix marks the change of word class
items.meaningCN: 缺口以及穿过缺口的通道；词性变化不靠后缀标记
items.example: The breakthrough came after ten years of work.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破在十年工作之后到来。

items.meaning: sudden pain that breaks through painkillers; the old literal sense applied to medicine
items.meaningCN: 突破止痛药控制的突发疼痛；旧字面义用于医学
items.example: She described the breakthrough pain as sharp and brief.
items.exampleCN: 她描述那种爆发痛尖锐而短暂。

items.meaning: an infection that gets past a vaccine or drug defence
items.meaningCN: 越过疫苗或药物防线的感染
items.example: Breakthrough infections are expected when a virus changes.
items.exampleCN: 病毒变异时，出现突破性感染是意料之中的。

items.meaning: the technology that produced the decisive advance
items.meaningCN: 产生决定性进展的技术
items.example: The breakthrough technology halved the cost of sequencing.
items.exampleCN: 这项突破性技术把测序成本降低了一半。

items.meaning: an escape or a sudden success beyond a former limit
items.meaningCN: 逃脱；突破原有局限的突然成功
items.example: The band had a breakout year after the album.
items.exampleCN: 这张专辑之后，乐队迎来了突破性的一年。

items.meaning: a collapse or a division into parts

items.meaning: the ending of a relationship or the splitting of a group

items.meaning: a separation or departure from a larger group

items.example: A breakaway faction formed a new party.
items.exampleCN: 一个脱离出来的派系组成了新政党。

latinEntries.meaning: a forward step; a Latin-derived counterpart, not the source of breakthrough
latinEntries.meaningCN: 前进一步；拉丁来源的对应词，并非 breakthrough 的来源

latinEntries.structure: Old French avancer, ultimately from Latin abante 'from before'
latinEntries.meaning: to move forward; again a counterpart rather than an ancestor
latinEntries.meaningCN: 向前移动；同样是对应词而非祖先

latinEntries.meaning: the introduction of something new; it stresses novelty, not a broken barrier
latinEntries.meaningCN: 引入新事物；强调新颖，而不是被打破的障碍

latinEntries.meaning: an uncovering, hence a find; it names the thing found, not the passage through a wall

definition_en: a soft round flat cap without a peak, usually of wool; a coloured cap worn by soldiers to show their unit
core_image: 画家把沾着颜料的扁圆软帽往脑后一推
scene: 画家把沾着颜料的贝雷帽往脑后一推。 The painter pushed his paint-stained beret back on his head.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：beret 指扁圆无檐的软帽；句意是画家把沾了颜料的贝雷帽往脑后推。

senses.title: The soft flat cap
senses.definition: a soft round cap with no peak, made of wool or felt and worn flat on the head
senses.definitionCN: 无檐的圆形软帽，用毛料或毡制，平戴在头上
senses.example: He rolled the beret and put it in his pocket.

senses.why: The word travelled from a hooded cloak to a head covering, and the cloak is long gone.
senses.whyCN: 该词从带风帽的斗篷转到头部覆盖物，而斗篷早已不在。

senses.title: The soldier cap
senses.definition: a coloured beret worn by a regiment as its badge of identity
senses.definitionCN: 以颜色标识部队身份的军用作训帽
senses.example: The green beret marked the unit before any badge.
senses.exampleCN: 在看清徽章之前，绿贝雷帽已经说明了兵种。
senses.why: Because the cap is plain, colour carries all the meaning, and armies turned it into a uniform sign.
senses.whyCN: 帽子本身素净，意义全由颜色承担，军队便把它变成了制服符号。

intro.en: Beret began as a hooded cloak, became a shepherd flat cap in the Pyrenees, and then a soldier badge of colour.
intro.cn: beret 起初是带风帽的斗篷，后来在比利牛斯成了牧人的扁帽，最后成为军中以色区分的标志。

items.en: Late Latin birrus names a thick cloak with a hood, probably a Celtic word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 birrus 指带风帽的厚斗篷，可能源自凯尔特语。

items.en: Medieval Latin birretum shifts from cloak to the head covering itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 birretum 由斗篷转为指头部覆盖物。

items.en: Gascon berret names a flat round cap worn by Basque and Pyrenean shepherds.
items.cn: 加斯科涅语 berret 指巴斯克与比利牛斯牧人戴的扁平圆帽。

items.en: French béret spreads the word as the Basque cap becomes widely worn.
items.cn: 法语 béret 随巴斯克帽的流行把该词传开。

items.en: French and British units adopt coloured berets, and the word enters army use.
items.cn: 法英部队采用彩色贝雷帽，该词进入军队用语。

items.en: English adopts the word for the soft flat cap, often with an artistic air.
items.cn: 英语借入该词指软扁圆帽，常带艺术气息。

entries.definitionCN: 长时间愤怒地斥责。

entries.definition: Deprived of something valued.
entries.definitionCN: 失去珍贵之物。

entries.definition: A pale green gem.
entries.definitionCN: 浅绿色宝石。

entries.definition: A small juicy fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 小而多汁的果实。

entries.definition: A soft head covering, often with a peak.

entries.definition: A hat tied under the chin.

entries.definition: A round wool cap with a pompom.

entries.definition: A red cylindrical hat with a tassel.
entries.definitionCN: 带流苏的红色圆柱帽。

normalIntro.en: Beret is a French word for a Basque shepherd cap. No peak, no brim, just a soft disc of wool.
normalIntro.cn: beret 是一个法语词，指巴斯克牧人的帽子。无檐、无舌，只是一片柔软的羊毛圆盘。

normal.en: No peak, no brim: you can fold it flat.
normal.cn: 无檐无舌，可以折平。

normal.en: French béret came from a Gascon word for the cap.
normal.cn: 法语 béret 出自加斯科涅语中的帽名。

normal.en: A green beret is a whole regiment in one colour.

normal.en: Berets is the plural, -s only.

normal.en: It began as a cloak with a hood, not a cap.
normal.cn: 它起初指带风帽的斗篷，而非帽子。

abstract.en: A circle of wool that tells you who someone is.
abstract.cn: 一片能说明你身份的羊毛圆盘。

abstract.en: Art worn where it can be seen.

examples.cn: 她在贝雷帽上别了一枚银胸针。

examples.en: The recruits were issued blue berets on day one.
examples.cn: 新兵第一天就领到了蓝色贝雷帽。

examples.en: He wore the beret pulled down over one ear.

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝蕾」——像一枚柔软的贝蕾圆片，无檐无舌，就是 beret 贝雷帽。联想两支场景：画家的沾色软帽，士兵的彩色军帽。

root: 经由法语 béret 上溯加斯科涅语 berret，再上溯中世纪拉丁语 birretum，最终到晚期拉丁语 birrus「带风帽的厚斗篷」，可能源自凯尔特语。19 世纪随巴斯克帽流行而西传，1918 年前后进入军队用语，1930 年代在英语中定型。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one cap: the plain wool disc everyone wears, and the coloured version an army uses as a name tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，同一顶帽：人人可戴的素色羊毛圆盘，以及军队当名牌用的彩色版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat wool disc pushed back off the forehead

branches.en: A paint mark on the wool.
branches.cn: 羊毛上的一处颜料。

branches.en: A beret rolled into a pocket.
branches.cn: 卷起来塞进口袋的贝雷帽。

branches.en: A green disc above a badge.
branches.cn: 徽章上方的一片绿。

branches.en: Recruits filing past with new caps.
branches.cn: 新兵戴着新帽列队走过。

branches.en: Shape first, colour later.
branches.cn: 先有形，后有颜色。

intro.en: Beret is a borrowed whole word; the useful parts are its Latin ancestor birrus and the small French endings around it.
intro.cn: beret 是整体借入的词；有用的构件是它的拉丁语祖先 birrus，以及围绕它的法语小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin birrus means a hooded cloak and Medieval Latin birretum means a cap; caput, head, is the other Latin thread here.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 birrus 意为带风帽的斗篷，中世纪拉丁语 birretum 意为帽；caput「头」是这里另一条拉丁线索。

definition_zh: 昼夜节律的；约一日周期的
definition_en: relating to biological rhythms that repeat about once every twenty-four hours
core_image: 一只看不见的钟嵌在细胞里，指针不由太阳直接推动，却每天与日出对一次表
scene: 夜班护士换了几轮班，身体仍按旧时间表在凌晨犯困。 Night-shift nurses often fight a circadian rhythm that never settles.
sceneCN: 这里 circadian 指「约一日重复的生物节律」（第 1 个义项：昼夜节律的）；句意为夜班护士常与一套始终无法安定的昼夜节律较劲。图中可辨识物件：护士站台灯、遮光窗帘、墙上的钟、打哈欠的侧脸。

pos.zh: 昼夜节律的；约一日周期的（通常作定语，如 circadian rhythm）

forms.label: 副词（按昼夜节律地，较少用）
同前缀形容词（约年周期的）
同前缀形容词（约潮汐周期的）
相关名词（昼夜节律紊乱）

derivatives.zh: circa（拉丁「大约」）+ annus（拉丁「年」）→ 约以一年为周期的
circa + tidal（潮汐的）→ 约以潮汐周期为节律的
circa + lunar（月亮的）→ 约以月相周期为节律的
circa + septan（七的，拉丁 septem）→ 约以七日为周期的
circa + semidian（半日的）→ 约以十二小时为周期的

senses.title: Repeating about once a day
senses.definition: describing a biological rhythm whose cycle length is close to twenty-four hours
senses.definitionCN: 形容周期长度接近二十四小时的生物节律
senses.example: Night-shift nurses often fight a circadian rhythm that never settles.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班护士常与一套始终无法安定的昼夜节律较劲。
senses.why: Circa is Latin for 'around' and dies for 'day', so circadian literally means 'about a day'.
senses.whyCN: circa 是拉丁语「大约」，dies 是「日」，因此 circadian 字面就是「约一日」。

senses.title: Belonging to the internal pacemaker
senses.definition: describing the internal clock tissue or circuit that generates the daily rhythm without outside help
senses.definitionCN: 形容在没有外界帮助时自行产生日节律的体内钟组织或回路
senses.example: The suprachiasmatic nucleus is the main circadian pacemaker in mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 视交叉上核是哺乳动物主要的昼夜节律起搏器。
senses.why: The rhythm persists in constant darkness, which shows that the clock is inside the body and not merely a response to sunrise.
senses.whyCN: 即使处于持续黑暗，节律仍然存在，这说明钟在体内，而不只是对日出的反应。

senses.title: Relating to clock genes and molecules
senses.titleCN: 与生物钟基因及分子回路有关的
senses.definition: describing the genes and proteins that form the feedback loop of the daily clock
senses.definitionCN: 形容构成日钟反馈回路的基因与蛋白质
senses.example: Circadian gene expression rises and falls in almost every tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 昼夜节律基因的表达在几乎所有组织中都起落。
senses.why: Once the clock was traced to molecules, the adjective attached itself to genes and proteins rather than to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 一旦钟被追溯到分子，这个形容词就附着于基因与蛋白质，而非行为。

senses.title: Of a phase within the daily cycle
senses.titleCN: 处于日循环某一时相的
senses.definition: describing a particular point in the cycle, such as the circadian phase of peak alertness
senses.definitionCN: 形容循环中的某一特定时点，如警觉高峰的昼夜节律时相
senses.example: Light in the evening shifts the circadian phase later.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的光把昼夜节律时相往后推。
senses.why: A cycle needs a reference point, so the adjective marks where on the dial an event happens.
senses.whyCN: 循环需要一个参照点，因此这个形容词标记事件发生在表盘上的哪个位置。

senses.title: Describing a disrupted rhythm
senses.titleCN: 形容节律被打乱的状态
senses.definition: describing the mismatch between an internal rhythm and the required schedule, as in shift work or jet lag
senses.definitionCN: 形容内部节律与所需日程之间的错配，如轮班或跨时区飞行
senses.example: Circadian disruption raises the risk of metabolic disease.
senses.exampleCN: 昼夜节律紊乱会提高代谢疾病的风险。
senses.why: Medicine uses the adjective for the harmful gap between body time and social time.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个形容词指「身体时间」与「社会时间」之间有害的落差。

senses.title: Running free under constant conditions
senses.titleCN: 在恒定条件下自由运行的
senses.definition: describing a rhythm that continues in constant darkness or constant light without daily resetting
senses.definitionCN: 形容在持续黑暗或持续光照中、不经每日重置仍继续的节律
senses.example: In constant darkness the circadian period drifts to about twenty-five hours.
senses.exampleCN: 在持续黑暗中，昼夜节律周期会漂移到约二十五小时。
senses.why: A free-running rhythm reveals the clock's own period, before the environment corrects it each day.
senses.whyCN: 自由运行节律显露钟自身的周期，也就是在被环境每天校正之前的样子。

senses.title: Rhythmic in hormone release or expression
senses.titleCN: 激素分泌或基因表达呈昼夜节律的
senses.definition: describing a substance or process that rises and falls on a daily schedule, as cortisol does
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种物质或过程按日节律起落，如皮质醇
senses.example: The circadian release of cortisol peaks just before waking.
senses.exampleCN: 皮质醇的昼夜节律释放会在醒来前达到高峰。
senses.why: The clock controls output, so the adjective can describe the rhythm of a hormone rather than the clock itself.
senses.whyCN: 钟控制输出，因此这个形容词可以描述激素的节律，而不只是钟本身。

senses.title: Mismatched after crossing time zones
senses.definition: describing the temporary misalignment between body time and local time after rapid travel
senses.definitionCN: 形容快速旅行后身体时间与当地时间暂时错位
senses.example: Circadian misalignment after a long flight leaves travellers groggy for days.
senses.exampleCN: 长途飞行后的昼夜节律错位让旅客迷糊好几天。
senses.why: The clock resets slowly, while the aircraft moves quickly, and the gap between them is what we feel as jet lag.
senses.whyCN: 钟重置得慢，飞机却移动得快，两者之间的落差就是我们感到的时差反应。

intro.en: Circadian was coined in 1959 by the chronobiologist Franz Halberg from Latin circa 'around, about' and dies 'day'. Both parts are Latin, but the compound itself is a modern scientific creation.
intro.cn: circadian 由时间生物学家弗朗茨·哈尔伯格于一九五九年用拉丁 circa「大约、围绕」与 dies「日」造出。两部分都是拉丁语，但复合词本身是近代科学新造。

items.en: Circa meant 'around, about', both as a preposition and as an approximation marker. It is related to circum 'around' and circus 'ring'.
items.cn: circa 意为「围绕、大约」，既作介词，也用来表示约数。它与 circum「环绕」、circus「圆圈」同源。

items.en: Dies meant 'day'. It survives in English in expressions such as per diem and in the Romance names for day.
items.cn: dies 意为「日、天」，在英语 per diem 等表达与罗曼语族表示「日」的词中留存。

items.en: Halberg proposed circadian in 1959 to name rhythms that cycle about once a day. The exact first publication date is well attested for this coinage.
items.cn: 哈尔伯格在一九五九年提出 circadian，用来命名约一日循环一次的节律。这一新造词的最早发表年代有明确记载。

items.en: The adjective spread from human rhythms to plants, insects and fungi as the same clock machinery was found across life.
items.cn: 随着同样的钟机制在各类生命中被发现，这个形容词从人体节律扩展到植物、昆虫与真菌。

items.en: Late twentieth-century genetics attached the word to clock genes and protein feedback loops.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的遗传学把这个词附着于钟基因与蛋白质反馈回路。

items.en: Sleep medicine and shift-work research made circadian disruption a standard clinical and occupational term.
items.cn: 睡眠医学与轮班研究使 circadian disruption 成为标准的临床与职业术语。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin circa element that are easy to confuse; group two holds words for regular time patterns.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 circa 成分、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示规律时间模式的词。

entries.definition: A Latin preposition meaning 'around, approximately', still used in English before dates; it is not an adjective for rhythms.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁介词，意为「大约、围绕」，英语中仍用于年代前；不是描述节律的形容词。

entries.definition: Circa plus annus 'year': a rhythm of about a year, such as seasonal breeding.
entries.definitionCN: circa 加 annus「年」：约以一年为周期的节律，如季节性繁殖。

entries.definition: Circa plus tidal: a rhythm of about twelve and a half hours, set by the tide rather than the sun.
entries.definitionCN: circa 加 tidal：约十二个半小时的节律，由潮汐而非太阳设定。

entries.definition: From Latin circuitus 'a going around', built on circumire; it names a path or an electrical loop, not a daily rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 circuitus「绕行」，由 circumire 构成；指路径或电路回路，而非日节律。

entries.definition: Active or happening in daylight hours; a diurnal animal may still have a circadian clock that runs at night.
entries.definitionCN: 在白天活动或发生；昼行动物仍可能有一套夜间运行的昼夜节律钟。

entries.definition: The plain word for 'every day'; it carries no claim about an internal clock.
entries.definitionCN: 「每天」的日常用词，不声称存在内部时钟。

entries.definition: Repeating in a regular pattern of any period, from seconds to seasons; circadian specifies about a day.
entries.definitionCN: 以任意周期规律重复，从秒到季节；circadian 特指约一日。

entries.definition: Occurring at regular intervals of any length; it does not imply a biological clock.
entries.definitionCN: 以任意长度的固定间隔发生；不暗示生物钟。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Circa 'about' plus dies 'day' gives 'about a day', which is exactly what the rhythm is.
normal.cn: circa「大约」加 dies「日」得出「约一日」，正是这种节律的样子。

normal.en: The family runs circadian, circannual, circatidal, circalunar, circaseptan, circasemidian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 circadian、circannual、circatidal、circalunar、circaseptan、circasemidian。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: circadian rhythm, circadian clock, circadian disruption, circadian phase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：昼夜节律、昼夜节律钟、节律紊乱、节律时相。

normal.en: A circadian rhythm survives in constant darkness, which proves the clock is internal.
normal.cn: 昼夜节律在持续黑暗中仍存在，这证明钟在体内。

normal.en: The word was coined as recently as 1959, so it has no ancient Latin original.
normal.cn: 这个词迟至一九五九年才被造出，因此没有古代拉丁原词。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket watch sealed in a dark box that still keeps time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封在暗盒里的怀表仍在走时。

abstract.en: Picture a plant lifting its leaves before sunrise, as if it had looked at a clock.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物在日出前抬起叶子，仿佛看过钟。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks in one room set twenty minutes apart.
abstract.cn: 想象同一房间里两只钟差了二十分钟。
