examples.cn: 夜班护士常与一套始终无法安定的昼夜节律较劲。

examples.en: Light in the evening shifts the circadian phase later.
examples.cn: 傍晚的光把昼夜节律时相往后推。

examples.en: In constant darkness the circadian period drifts to about twenty-five hours.
examples.cn: 在持续黑暗中，昼夜节律周期会漂移到约二十五小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「circa 大约 + di 日」——大约一日一轮回 → 昼夜节律的

root: 拉丁 circa「大约、围绕」+ 拉丁 dies「日」，字面即「约一日」；该词由哈尔伯格于一九五九年新造，无古代拉丁原词。英语 circadian。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loop: a body keeps its own roughly daily time. The loop is first the rhythm, then the pacemaker, its genes, its phase, its failures and its misalignment with the world.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个回路展开：身体自带一套约一日的计时。这个回路先是节律，再是起搏器、其基因、其时相、其失灵，以及它与外部世界的错位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unseen clock inside a cell, checked daily against sunrise.
core.cn: 核心意象：细胞里一只看不见的钟，每天与日出对表。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM AND ITS SOURCE: the daily cycle and the tissue that generates it.
branches.cn: 节律与来源：日循环本身，以及产生它的组织。

branches.en: MOLECULAR CLOCK: genes and proteins form the loop that keeps the beat.
branches.cn: 分子钟：基因与蛋白质构成维持节拍的回路。

branches.en: POSITION AND OUTPUT: the adjective marks where on the dial an event sits and which hormone follows it.
branches.cn: 位置与输出：这个形容词标记事件在表盘上的位置，以及随之分泌的激素。

branches.en: BROKEN ALIGNMENT: disruption and jet lag are the same gap between body time and required time.
branches.cn: 错位：节律紊乱与时差反应，都是身体时间与要求时间之间的同一道落差。

branches.en: FREE RUNNING: constant conditions reveal the clock's own period.
branches.cn: 自由运行：恒定条件显露钟自身的周期。

intro.en: Circadian is a modern Latin compound; its first element also builds a small family of rhythm words, while the second element is simply the Latin word for day.
intro.cn: circadian 是近代拉丁复合词；前一成分还构成一小族节律词，后一成分就是拉丁语「日」。

latinIntro.en: Latin circa 'around' and dies 'day' make the adjective; circa also combines with annus, lunar and septem to name other biological cycles.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 circa「大约」与 dies「日」构成这个形容词；circa 还与 annus、lunar、septem 组合，命名其他生物周期。

items.example: The circadian cycle is about twenty-four hours.
items.exampleCN: 昼夜节律周期约为二十四小时。

items.meaningCN: 以昼夜节律方式（较少用）
items.example: The tissue responds circadianly to light.
items.exampleCN: 该组织以昼夜节律方式对光作出反应。

items.example: Circannual clocks time the breeding season.
items.exampleCN: 约年周期的钟安排繁殖季。

items.example: Crabs show a circatidal activity pattern.
items.exampleCN: 螃蟹表现出约潮汐周期的活动模式。

items.example: Corals spawn on a circalunar rhythm.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚按约月相节律产卵。

items.example: A circaseptan rhythm appears in some patients.
items.exampleCN: 某些病人身上出现约七日的节律。

items.meaningCN: 约以十二小时为周期的
items.example: A circasemidian rest break splits the day.
items.exampleCN: 一次约半日的休息把一天分成两段。

definition_zh: 最佳的；最优的；最适宜的
definition_en: best possible under the given conditions; most favourable
core_image: 一把尺子量到刚刚好，不多一格，也不少一格
scene: 调参的人把三组数值来回试了十几遍，最后停在中间那一组。 That setting gives optimal performance without extra heat.
sceneCN: 这里指各种条件配合到最好（第 1 个义项：在现有条件下最好的结果）；句意为那组设置带来最佳性能，还不会额外发热。

pos.zh: 最佳的；最优的；最适宜的

senses.title: The best possible result
senses.definition: the best outcome available under the present limits
senses.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能得到的最好结果
senses.example: The team reached an optimal result with the given budget.
senses.exampleCN: 团队用既定预算取得了最佳结果。
senses.why: Optimus is the Latin superlative of good, so the word names the top of a scale rather than a direction.
senses.whyCN: optimus 是拉丁语「好」的最高级，因此这个词命名刻度的顶点，而不是某个方向。

senses.title: The most favourable conditions
senses.definition: the conditions under which a process works best
senses.definitionCN: 某过程运作得最好的条件
senses.example: The plants grow at optimal temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物在最适温度下生长。
senses.why: Once the top of the scale is a point, conditions can be tuned to that point.
senses.whyCN: 一旦刻度的顶点成了一个点，条件就可以调到那一点。

senses.title: A mathematical optimum
senses.definition: a point where a function reaches its best value
senses.definitionCN: 函数取得最好值的点
senses.example: The algorithm searches for an optimal point on the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 算法在曲线上寻找一个最优点。
senses.why: Calculus formalised the everyday top of a scale as a stationary best value.
senses.whyCN: 微积分把日常说的「顶点」形式化为一个驻定的最优值。

senses.title: An efficient economic allocation
senses.definition: the arrangement that uses resources with the least waste
senses.definitionCN: 以最少浪费使用资源的安排
senses.example: The market reached an optimal allocation of labour.
senses.exampleCN: 市场达到了劳动力的最优配置。
senses.why: Economics measures the top by output per unit of input.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用每单位投入的产出来衡量这个顶点。

senses.title: The best dose or timing for the body
senses.titleCN: 对身体最合适的剂量或时机
senses.definition: the amount or moment that does most good and least harm
senses.definitionCN: 收益最大、伤害最小的用量或时点
senses.example: The trial looked for the optimal dose.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验寻找最佳剂量。
senses.why: Medicine turns the scale into a trade-off between benefit and harm.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个刻度变成收益与伤害之间的权衡。

senses.title: A settled engineering trade-off
senses.titleCN: 工程上权衡后的最优点
senses.definition: the design point where competing requirements balance best
senses.definitionCN: 各项相争的要求平衡得最好的设计点
senses.example: Weight and strength meet at an optimal thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 重量与强度在某个最佳厚度上取得平衡。
senses.why: Engineering makes the top a compromise rather than a single peak.
senses.whyCN: 工程学让这个顶点成为折中，而不是孤峰。

senses.title: A biological best fit
senses.definition: the behaviour or form that suits an environment best
senses.definitionCN: 最适应某环境的行为或形态
senses.example: The birds show optimal foraging in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在冬季表现出最优觅食。
senses.why: Biology asks what a body or habit is best fitted to, not what is morally best.
senses.whyCN: 生物学问的是身体或习性最适合什么，而非什么在道德上最好。

senses.title: The sensible everyday choice
senses.titleCN: 日常判断中的最佳选择
senses.definition: the choice a careful person judges best overall
senses.definitionCN: 谨慎的人综合判断后认为最好的选择
senses.example: Leaving early was the optimal decision given the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 考虑到交通，早走是最佳决定。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the superlative for a reasoned preference.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言借这个最高级表达有理由的偏好。

intro.en: Optimal comes from Latin optimus, best, the suppletive superlative of bonus, good, with the English suffix -al. The direct source is clear; the deeper origin of optimus is a hypothesis.
intro.cn: optimal 来自拉丁 optimus「最好的」，它是 bonus「好的」的补充式最高级，再加英语后缀 -al。直接来源清楚；optimus 更深的来源是一种假说。

items.en: Bonus meant good, but its comparative melior and superlative optimus came from other stems, a suppletion familiar from good, better, best.
items.cn: bonus 意为好的，但其比较级 melior 与最高级 optimus 来自别的词干，这种补充式与英语 good、better、best 相似。

items.en: Optimus served as best and as most excellent in rank.
items.cn: optimus 既作「最好的」，也指品级上最卓越的。

items.en: Optimus is often connected with ops, resources or power, which would make the earliest sense richest or most able; the derivation is source uncertain.
items.cn: optimus 常与 ops「资源、力量」相联系，若如此则最早义为「最富足」或「最有能力」；这一派生来源不确定。

items.en: The neuter optimum was borrowed as a noun for the best value, especially in mathematics.
items.cn: 中性形式 optimum 被借作名词，指最佳值，尤用于数学。

items.en: English built optimal on optimus in the nineteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪用 optimus 造出 optimal，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Optimisation, suboptimal and optimal control extend the word without changing its peak sense.
items.cn: 最优化、次优与最优控制都沿用这个词，未改变其「顶点」义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin best-stem; the second group names what sits at the top of a scale.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「最好」的词干；第二组是处在刻度顶端的近义说法。

entries.definition: The best value or point, especially in mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 最佳值或最优点，尤用于数学。

entries.definition: The belief that things tend toward the best; coined from the Latin optimum.
entries.definitionCN: 相信事物趋向最好的看法；由拉丁 optimum 造出。

entries.definition: To make something as good as it can be; built on optimum.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能好；由 optimum 构成。

entries.definition: Below the best level, built with the prefix sub-.
entries.definitionCN: 低于最佳水平，由前缀 sub- 构成。

entries.definition: Expecting the best outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 期待最好结果。

entries.definition: The highest in quality or rank; the plain English word.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或等级最高的；最平实的英语说法。

entries.definition: Perfect in an imagined standard, sometimes unattainable.
entries.definitionCN: 符合想象标准的完美，有时难以达到。

entries.definition: Helpful to a plan or outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 对计划或结果有利的。

entries.definition: Of the best quality or at the best moment.
entries.definitionCN: 质量最好的或时机最佳的。

entries.definition: The highest point reached.
entries.definitionCN: 达到的最高点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin superlative, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁最高级、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Optimus is the superlative of bonus, just as best is the superlative of good.
normal.cn: optimus 是 bonus 的最高级，正如英语中「最好」是「好」的最高级。

normal.en: Optimum is the noun for the best value; optimal is the adjective.
normal.cn: optimum 是「最佳值」的名词，optimal 是形容词。

normal.en: The ops hypothesis would make optimus mean richest before it meant best.
normal.cn: 若按 ops 假说，optimus 最早是「最富足」，后来才成「最好」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sense: optimal performance, optimal conditions, optimal dose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：最佳性能、最适条件、最佳剂量。

normal.en: Suboptimal is the useful opposite for anything below the best.
normal.cn: suboptimal 是表示「未达最佳」的常用反义说法。

abstract.en: Optimal is a ruler that stops exactly at the mark, with no spare space.
abstract.cn: 最优是一把正好停在刻度上的尺子，不留多余空隙。

abstract.en: There can be only one top of a scale, which is why the word tolerates no better.
abstract.cn: 一个刻度只能有一个顶点，所以这个词容不下「更好」。

abstract.en: In engineering the peak is a compromise, not a triumph.
abstract.cn: 在工程里，顶点是折中，而不是凯旋。

examples.en: The optimal route avoids both the tunnel and the rush hour.
examples.cn: 最优路线既避开隧道，也避开高峰时段。

examples.en: An optimal diet is not the same for every patient.
examples.cn: 最佳饮食对每位病人并不相同。

examples.en: The engine runs at optimal speed only in cool air.
examples.cn: 这台发动机只在凉爽空气中才以最佳转速运行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧普提莫」——挑到最顶上那一个：最佳的

root: 拉丁 optimus「最好的」，是 bonus「好的」的补充式最高级；更深来源一般认为与 ops「资源、力量」相关，亦有「最高处」的解释，词根来源不确定。中性 optimum 先作名词「最佳值」，英语十九世纪再加 -al 构成形容词，确切首见年代不确定；suboptimal 由 sub- 加 optimal 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the best result through conditions, mathematics, economics, medicine, engineering and biology to the ordinary reasoned choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最好的结果出发，经条件、数学、经济、医学、工程与生物学，最后落到日常有理由的选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler that stops exactly at the mark, no spare space either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把正好停在刻度上的尺子，两边都不留余地。

branches.en: THE BEST RESULT: the highest outcome the limits allow.
branches.cn: 最好的结果：条件允许范围内的最高结果。

branches.en: THE TUNED CONDITIONS AND THE WISE CHOICE: the setting that suits a process and the choice a person judges best.
branches.cn: 调好的条件与明智的选择：适合某过程的环境，以及人判断为最好的选择。

branches.en: THE MATHEMATICAL POINT: where a function reaches its best value.
branches.cn: 数学上的点：函数取得最优值之处。

branches.en: THE BALANCED ALLOCATION: resources used without waste and a design trade-off settled.
branches.cn: 平衡的配置：资源无浪费地使用，设计权衡得以定案。

branches.en: THE BEST FIT FOR A BODY: the dose that helps most and the habit that suits an environment.
branches.cn: 对身体的最佳适配：收益最大的剂量与最适应环境的习性。

intro.en: Optimal is the Latin best-stem optimus plus the English suffix -al; its noun optimum and its opposite suboptimal came later.
intro.cn: optimal 是拉丁语「最好」词干 optimus 加英语后缀 -al；名词 optimum 与反义形式 suboptimal 都后起。

latinIntro.en: Optimus supplies the superlative, ops is the disputed deeper connection, and optimum supplies the noun.
latinIntro.cn: optimus 提供最高级，ops 是有争议的更深关联，optimum 提供名词。

items.example: The superlative closes the scale at the top.
items.exampleCN: 最高级把刻度封在顶端。

items.example: Bonus supplies the positive that optimus replaces.
items.exampleCN: bonus 提供由 optimus 顶替的原级。

items.example: The disputed connection would make best originally richest.
items.exampleCN: 有争议的关联会让「最好」最早意为「最富足」。

items.structure: Latin neuter adjective used as noun
items.example: Mathematics borrowed the neuter as a noun.
items.exampleCN: 数学把这个中性形式借作名词。

items.example: English adds -al to the Latin stem.
The adverb marks the manner of reaching the peak.
items.exampleCN: 副词标出达到顶点的方式。

items.example: The noun belongs to mathematics and economics.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词属于数学与经济学。

items.meaning: to make as good as possible
items.example: The verb is built on optimum, not on optimal.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词由 optimum 构成，不是由 optimal。

items.example: The prefix names a level below the best.
items.exampleCN: 前缀命名低于最佳的水平。

items.example: It also builds final, formal and general.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 final、formal 与 general。

definition_zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的
definition_en: relating to a market dominated by a few sellers
core_image: 棋盘上只留下四枚同色棋子，其余格子空着，四枚棋子互相牵制
scene: 棋盘上只剩四枚同色棋子，彼此隔着几格，谁也不肯先动。 The airline industry remains oligopolistic despite repeated attempts at liberalization.
sceneCN: 这里 oligopolistic 指「由少数卖方主导的」（第 1 个义项：具有寡头市场结构特征的）；句意为尽管多次推动自由化，航空业仍呈寡头格局。图中可辨识物件：四枚同色棋子、空棋盘格、相互牵制的距离、未动的棋子。

pos.zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的

senses.title: Having the shape of few-seller market
senses.titleCN: 呈少数卖方市场形态的
senses.definition: describing a market whose supply is concentrated in a small number of firms
senses.definitionCN: 描述供给集中在少数几家企业的市场
senses.example: The telecom sector has an oligopolistic shape.
senses.exampleCN: 电信行业呈寡头形态。
senses.why: oligopoly plus -istic gives the adjective of resemblance, parallel to monopolistic.
senses.whyCN: oligopoly 加 -istic 构成表示相似的形容词，与 monopolistic 平行。

senses.title: Pricing by a few sellers
senses.definition: describing prices set by a small group that watches one another
senses.definitionCN: 描述由相互观望的小群体设定的价格
senses.example: Oligopolistic pricing kept fares almost equal across the three airlines.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头定价使三家航空公司的票价几乎相同。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the price behaviour that the structure produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于该结构所产生的价格行为。

senses.title: Rivalry among the few
senses.definition: describing competition in which each move is answered by the others
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种每一步都被其余几家回应的竞争
senses.example: Oligopolistic competition runs through advertising rather than price.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头竞争通过广告而非价格展开。
senses.why: with few players, every action is visible, so rivalry becomes a sequence of responses.
senses.whyCN: 参与者少，每个动作都可见，竞争便成为一连串回应。

senses.title: Given to tacit collusion
senses.definition: describing a market where the few can align without a formal agreement
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家无需正式协议就能取得一致的市场
senses.example: The regulator found oligopolistic coordination in fuel surcharges.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者发现燃油附加费存在寡头式协同。
senses.why: the adjective can describe behaviour as well as structure, and collusion is the behaviour most feared.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既可描述结构也可描述行为，而合谋是最受担忧的行为。

senses.title: Belonging to a highly concentrated industry
senses.definition: describing an industry where the top few hold most of the market
senses.definitionCN: 描述前几家占有大部分市场的产业
senses.example: The rating agencies form an oligopolistic industry of three firms.
senses.exampleCN: 评级机构构成由三家企业组成的寡头产业。
senses.why: concentration ratios give the adjective a measurable threshold in industrial economics.
senses.whyCN: 集中度比率在产业经济学中给这个形容词一个可测量的门槛。

senses.title: Behind high entry barriers
senses.titleCN: 处于高进入壁垒之后的
senses.definition: describing a market where the few are protected by costs or rules that block newcomers
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家受成本或规则保护、新来者难以进入的市场
senses.example: An oligopolistic market can persist because new refineries are too expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头市场能够持续，因为新建炼厂过于昂贵。
senses.why: the few survive only while entry stays hard, so the adjective often implies a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 只有当进入仍然困难时少数几家才能存活，因此这个形容词常含壁垒之意。

senses.title: As regulators describe a sector
senses.titleCN: 监管者描述某一行业时的用语
senses.definition: the label competition authorities use for a sector they consider too concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 竞争主管机构用来指称其认为过于集中的行业的标签
senses.example: The report called the funeral market oligopolistic and recommended review.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称殡葬市场为寡头市场，并建议审查。
senses.why: legal usage prefers the adjective because it describes a condition without alleging a specific violation.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法偏好这个形容词，因为它描述一种状态，而不指控具体违法行为。

senses.title: Held by a few in any field
senses.titleCN: 任何领域由少数把持的
senses.definition: describing any domain where a handful of actors control access
senses.definitionCN: 描述任何由少数行为者控制准入的领域
senses.example: The awards circuit remains oligopolistic, with four studios taking most nominations.
senses.exampleCN: 评奖圈仍呈寡头格局，四家制片厂拿走大部分提名。
senses.why: the adjective leaves economics once access anywhere is controlled by a small group.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何领域的准入被小群体控制，这个形容词就走出经济学。

intro.en: Oligopolistic is an English derivative of oligopoly, formed with the suffix complex -ist plus -ic, the same pattern as monopolistic. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oligopolistic 是 oligopoly 的英语派生词，由 -ist 加 -ic 的后缀组合构成，与 monopolistic 同一模式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oligos 'few' supplies the first element, the same root that opens oligarchy.
items.cn: oligos「少数」提供第一成分，与 oligarchy 开头同一词根。

items.en: Pōlein 'to sell' supplies the second element, unchanged from monopoly and duopoly.
items.cn: pōlein「卖」提供第二成分，与 monopoly、duopoly 中相同。

items.en: The noun was coined in late nineteenth-century economics on the model of monopoly.
items.cn: 这个名词于 19 世纪后期仿 monopoly 在经济学中造出。

items.en: English added -ist for a participant and -ic for the relating adjective, so oligopolist came before oligopolistic.
items.cn: 英语先加 -ist 表示参与者，再加 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此 oligopolist 先于 oligopolistic。

items.en: The adjective appears in twentieth-century industrial economics, once concentration ratios made few-seller markets measurable.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在 20 世纪产业经济学中，当时集中度比率使少数卖方市场变得可测量。

items.en: The exact first printed use is not recorded. The suffix chain is fully documented and the Greek elements are attested.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例没有确切记录。后缀链条有完整书证，希腊成分也有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same compound and one same-root look-alike; group two holds adjectives that describe concentration or exclusion without naming the structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该复合词的词形，以及一个同根形近词；第二组是描述集中或排除、却不指称该结构的形容词。

entries.definition: The structure itself; oligopolistic is the adjective that describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 结构本身；oligopolistic 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: The parallel adjective for a single dominant seller; the suffix is the same, the first element is not.
entries.definitionCN: 平行形容词，用于单一支配卖方；后缀相同，第一成分不同。

entries.definition: From oligos plus archein 'to rule', meaning governed by a small group; its second element is political, not commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 oligos 加 archein「统治」，意为由小群体治理；第二成分是政治的，而非商业的。

entries.definition: The adjective for exactly two sellers, the narrowest case of an oligopolistic market.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好两家卖方的形容词，是寡头市场中最窄的情形。

entries.definition: Describing a market where a large share sits with few firms; concentration is a measure, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述很大份额集中于少数企业的市场；集中度是一种度量，而非结构。

entries.definition: Describing an industry organized through agreements; an oligopolistic market may be cartelized, but not all are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述通过协议组织起来的产业；寡头市场可能被卡特尔化，但并非全都如此。

entries.definition: Describing terms that do not reflect rivalry; it names the result, while oligopolistic names the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不反映竞争的条款；它指结果，而 oligopolistic 指结构。

entries.definition: Describing practices that limit what others may do; restrictive conduct can occur in a market that is not oligopolistic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述限制他人可为之事的行为；限制性行为也可发生在非寡头市场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oligopoly + -ist + -ic: the adjective of the few-seller structure.
normal.cn: oligopoly + -ist + -ic：少数卖方结构的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs oligopoly, oligopolist, oligopolistically, duopoly, monopoly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oligopoly、oligopolist、oligopolistically、duopoly、monopoly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: oligopolistic market, oligopolistic pricing, oligopolistic competition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：寡头市场、寡头定价、寡头竞争。

normal.en: Its parallel is monopolistic: same suffix, first element changed from one to few.
normal.cn: 它的平行词是 monopolistic：后缀相同，第一成分从「一」变为「少数」。

normal.en: The look-alike oligarchic uses the root for rule, not the root for selling.
normal.cn: 形近词 oligarchic 用的是「统治」词根，而非「卖」词根。

abstract.en: Picture four pieces on a board with every other square empty.
abstract.cn: 想象棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，其余格子全空。

abstract.en: Picture four doors on one corridor and no other corridor to enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊上只有四扇门，没有别的走廊可进。

abstract.en: Picture four prices written on one board in the same handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象四家价格写在同一块牌上，笔迹都一样。

examples.en: The market for operating systems is oligopolistic rather than open.
examples.cn: 操作系统市场呈寡头格局，而非开放市场。

examples.en: Oligopolistic pricing can keep margins high even when demand falls.
examples.cn: 即使需求下降，寡头定价也能维持较高利润率。

examples.en: Regulators described the fuel retail sector as highly oligopolistic.
examples.cn: 监管者称燃油零售业高度寡头化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oligopoly（寡头）+ istic（……的）」——少数几家说了算的 → 寡头垄断的

root: oligopoly（希腊 oligos「少数」+ pōlein「卖」，仿 monopoly 于 19 世纪后期造出）+ 后缀 -ist + -ic，构成「寡头市场特征的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one small group: a market takes the shape of few sellers, and that shape is then read as structure, pricing, rivalry, coordination, concentration, barriers, regulatory label, and finally any field held by a few.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个小群体展开：市场呈现出少数卖方的形状，这个形状再被读作结构、定价、竞争、协同、集中度、壁垒、监管标签，最后是任何由少数把持的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four pieces left on a board, each watching the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，彼此盯着对方。

branches.en: SHAPE AND PRICE: the few-seller form, and the prices it produces.
branches.cn: 形态与价格：少数卖方的形态，以及它所产生的价格。

branches.en: RIVALRY AND COORDINATION: moves answered move by move, and the quiet alignment that can follow.
branches.cn: 竞争与协同：一步被一步回应，以及随后可能出现的安静一致。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: the top few hold most of the market.
branches.cn: 集中度：前几家握住大部分市场。

branches.en: BARRIERS AND LABEL: newcomers blocked by cost, and the word regulators put on the sector.
branches.cn: 壁垒与标签：新来者被成本挡住，以及监管者贴在该行业上的词。

branches.en: ANY SMALL CIRCLE: four studios, four clubs, any field held by a handful.
branches.cn: 任何小圈子：四家制片厂、四家俱乐部，任何被少数把持的领域。

intro.en: The adjective piles an English suffix complex onto a Greek-style compound, so the compound and the ending can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在一个希腊式复合词上叠了英语后缀组合，因此复合词与词尾可以分开读。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base word here; the pattern of -isticus came through French from Greek -istikos, while oligos and pōlein remain Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁基础词；-isticus 的模式经法语来自希腊 -istikos，而 oligos 与 pōlein 仍是希腊语。

items.example: The element also appears in oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 oligarchy 中。

items.example: The selling element stays unchanged across the family.
items.exampleCN: 「卖」这个成分在整个词族中保持不变。

items.example: Each oligopolist matched the rival's cut.
items.exampleCN: 每个寡头都跟随对手降价。
这三家企业以寡头方式定价。

items.example: The duopolistic route raised fares together.
items.exampleCN: 这条双寡头航线一起提价。

items.example: The club had an oligarchic board.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部有一个寡头式董事会。

definition_zh: 司法的；法院的；法官的；审判上的；审慎公正的
definition_en: relating to courts, judges or the deciding of cases, and sometimes meaning carefully fair
core_image: 一份裁定书首页盖着法院的印章，正文第一句就写明「本院认为」
scene: 裁定书送到时，双方都先翻到最后一页看结论，再回头看理由。 The judicial review found the order unlawful.
sceneCN: 这里 judicial 指属于法院审查程序的（第 3 个义项：司法审查的）；句意为司法审查认定该命令不合法。

pos.zh: 司法的；法院的；审判的
审慎公正的（多见于 judicial temperament 一类说法）

derivatives.zh: 司法系统（judicial + -ary「机构」，由属性转指持有它的机关）
以司法方式（judicial + -ly，由属性转指方式）
明智的（与 judicial 同出 iudicium，但走的是「判断力」一路）
有害的；有偏见的（prae-「在前」+ iudicium，由「预先裁断」转指不利影响）

senses.title: Of the courts
senses.definition: belonging to the court system as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为机构的法院体系
senses.example: The judicial system handles ten thousand claims a year.
senses.exampleCN: 司法系统每年处理一万件请求。
senses.why: the Latin adjective meant 'of a judge', and English widened it to the whole court apparatus.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「法官的」，英语把它扩到整个法院机器。

senses.title: Of a judge's work
senses.definition: concerning the act of hearing and deciding a case
senses.definitionCN: 关于听审并裁定案件的行为
senses.example: Judicial discretion is narrow where the rule is clear.
senses.exampleCN: 规则清楚之处，法官的裁量空间很小。
senses.why: the core sense stays with the person who declares the law, not with the building.
senses.whyCN: 核心义仍系于宣告法律的那个人，而非建筑。

senses.title: Judicial review
senses.definition: concerning a court's power to strike down acts of other branches
senses.definitionCN: 关于法院推翻其他分支行为的权力
senses.example: The judicial review found the order unlawful.
senses.exampleCN: 司法审查认定该命令不合法。
senses.why: review makes the adjective name a specific power rather than a general quality.
senses.whyCN: 「审查」这一搭配使这个形容词指一项具体权力，而非一般性质。

senses.title: Of a ruling
senses.definition: issued by a court in the form of a binding decision
senses.definitionCN: 由法院以有约束力的决定形式发出
senses.example: A judicial order stopped the eviction for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 一项司法命令把驱逐推迟了一个月。
senses.why: once issued, a decision carries the authority of the bench that made it.
senses.whyCN: 一经发出，决定便带上作出它的法官席的权威。

senses.title: Fair and deliberate
senses.definition: showing the calm, even-handed manner expected of a judge
senses.definitionCN: 显出法官应有的沉着与不偏不倚
senses.example: She answered with a judicial calm that annoyed the questioner.
senses.exampleCN: 她以司法者般的沉着作答，反倒惹恼了提问者。
senses.why: the manner of judging became a personal virtue, so the adjective can describe a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 裁断的作风成了一种个人德性，因此形容词可描述性情。

senses.title: By court order
senses.titleCN: 由法院裁定的、司法裁定的
senses.definition: imposed or authorized by a court rather than by an agency
senses.definitionCN: 由法院而非行政机关施加或授权
senses.example: The records were released under judicial compulsion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些记录是在司法强制下公布的。
senses.why: the adjective marks the source of authority, separating court orders from administrative ones.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标示权威来源，把法院命令与行政命令分开。

senses.title: One of three functions
senses.definition: naming the third function of government in the doctrine of separation of powers
senses.definitionCN: 在三权分立学说中指政府的第三项职能
senses.example: Judicial independence is written into the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 司法独立被写入宪法。
senses.why: constitutional language needs three parallel adjectives, and this one is defined by contrast.
senses.whyCN: 宪制语言需要三个并列形容词，这一个靠对照定义。

senses.title: Of procedure
senses.definition: concerning the steps by which a dispute is heard and decided
senses.definitionCN: 关于听审并裁定争议所经的步骤
senses.example: Judicial delay hurts claimants more than defendants.
senses.exampleCN: 司法拖延对索赔者的伤害大于对被告。
senses.why: procedure is the observable face of judging, so the adjective attaches to it naturally.
senses.whyCN: 程序是裁断可见的那一面，因此形容词自然附上去。

intro.en: Judicial comes from Latin iudicialis, from iudicium 'judgment', from iudex 'judge', built on ius 'law, right' and dicere 'to say'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: judicial 来自拉丁 iudicialis，上溯 iudicium「裁断」，再上溯 iudex「法官」，由 ius「法、权利」与 dicere「说」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ius 'law, right' has no established deeper origin; the suggestion of a link to iurare 'to swear' remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: ius「法、权利」的更深来源未得到证明；与 iurare「发誓」有关的说法仍属假说。

items.en: Ius plus dicere produced iudex, literally one who declares what is lawful, and iudicium, the declaring itself.
items.cn: ius 加 dicere 构成 iudex，字面即宣告何为合法者，以及 iudicium，即这一宣告本身。

items.en: Iudicialis meant 'of a judge or a trial', the adjective of iudicium, and it passed through French into English.
items.cn: iudicialis 意为「法官的、审判的」，是 iudicium 的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: English took judicial in the sixteenth century, first for the deciding of cases and soon for the whole court system.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 judicial，先指案件的裁断，不久也指整个法院体系。

items.en: Judicious, built on the same iudicium but with -ous, kept the sense of good judgement, while judicial kept the institutional sense.
items.cn: judicious 同出 iudicium 但带 -ous，保留「判断力好」之义；judicial 则保留机构义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not exactly dated, and the origin of ius is unsettled, so older forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证没有确切年代；ius 的来源无定论，为其提出的更早形式属重构形式。

note.en: Group one shares the iudicium stem; group two holds near neighbours in legal description.
note.cn: 第一组共享 iudicium 词干；第二组是法律描述上的近义词。

entries.definition: The courts or judges as an institution; judicial describes what belongs to them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为机构的法院或法官；judicial 描述属于它们之物。

entries.definition: Sensible and prudent, a quality of decisions; it is not a synonym of judicial despite the shared stem.
entries.definitionCN: 明智审慎，是决定的品质；虽共享词干，却非 judicial 的同义词。

entries.definition: From Latin iuridicus, ius plus dicere again, but through a different adjective; it means relating to law as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 iuridicus，仍是 ius 加 dicere，却经另一形容词；意为与法律体系有关的。

entries.definition: Concerning law as a body of rules, including statutes and contracts; judicial is narrower and points at courts.
entries.definitionCN: 关于作为规则总体的法律，含法令与合同；judicial 更窄，指向法院。

entries.definition: Used before a noun for what belongs to a tribunal, as in a court order; judicial is the formal equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 置于名词前指属于法庭之物，如法院命令；judicial 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: Of the process of hearing and ruling; judicial also covers the institution, not only the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指听审与裁定的过程；judicial 还涵盖机构，不限于行为。

entries.definition: Of evidence and argument in court; it is technical and evidential where judicial is institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 指法庭上的证据与论证；偏技术与证据，而 judicial 偏机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ius 'law' + dicere 'say': judicial work is saying what the law already requires.
normal.cn: ius「法」+ dicere「说」：司法工作就是说出法律已经要求的东西。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the power: judicial review, judicial power, judicial independence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出权力：司法审查、司法权、司法独立。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judiciary, judicial, judicious, prejudicial, adjudicate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judiciary、judicial、judicious、prejudicial、adjudicate。

normal.en: Keep the pair apart: judicial is the bench, judicious is the good sense behind a decision.
normal.cn: 把这一对分开：judicial 是法官席，judicious 是决定背后的明智。

normal.en: Judicially is the adverb: the claim was judicially resolved.
normal.cn: 副词是 judicially：该请求经司法途径解决。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp that turns an opinion into something the whole country must obey.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章，把一段意见变成全国都得服从的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a judge who speaks last, after everyone else has spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象一位最后发言的法官，别人都说完他才开口。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that must be visibly level, or the room stops trusting it.
abstract.cn: 想象一架必须让人看见它平的天平，否则整个房间就不再信它。

examples.en: The judicial branch cannot write its own budget.
examples.cn: 司法分支无法自己写预算。

examples.en: A judicial inquiry cleared the officer but criticized the practice.
examples.cn: 一项司法调查洗清了这位警官，却批评了那套做法。

examples.en: Judicial appointments became the centre of the debate.
examples.cn: 司法任命成了辩论的中心。

dict_mnemonic.text: jud（法）+ icial（……的）＝ 与法官席有关的；记「法院盖章，judicious 是脑子清楚」。

root: 拉丁 iudicialis ← iudicium「裁断」← iudex「法官」= ius「法、权利」（更深来源不确定）+ dicere「说、宣告」；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle one bench: the court system, a judge at work, review of other branches, a binding order, a fair manner, a court-authorized act, the third function of government, and the procedure that carries it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围着一张法官席：法院体系、法官在工作、审查其他分支、有约束力的命令、公正作风、经法院授权的行为、政府第三项职能，以及承载它的程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruling sheet stamped with a court seal, beginning with the words the court holds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份盖着法院印章的裁定书，开头写着「本院认为」。

branches.en: BUILDING AND BENCH: the institution, then the person deciding inside it.
branches.cn: 楼与席：先是机构，再是在其中裁断的人。

branches.en: POWER AND ITS INSTRUMENT: review, then the order that carries the result.
branches.cn: 权力与其工具：审查，以及承载结果的命令。

branches.en: MANNER AS VIRTUE: the judge's calm becomes an admired personal quality.
branches.cn: 作风成德：法官的沉着变成一种被赞赏的个人品质。

branches.en: SOURCE OF AUTHORITY: court-authorized, as against administrative.
branches.cn: 权威来源：法院授权，与行政相对。

branches.en: THE THIRD FUNCTION AND ITS STEPS: one constitutional branch, and the procedure that makes it visible.
branches.cn: 第三职能与步骤：一个宪制分支，以及使它可见的程序。

intro.en: Judicial is a Latin adjective in -alis built on a noun of judging, and both parts recur throughout legal English.
intro.cn: judicial 是 -alis 结尾的拉丁形容词，建立在表示裁断的名词上，两部分在法律英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Iudicium gives judicial, judicious and prejudice; iudex gives judge and judgment; dicere gives verdict, predict and dictate.
latinIntro.cn: iudicium 衍生 judicial、judicious、prejudice；iudex 衍生 judge、judgment；dicere 衍生 verdict、predict、dictate。

items.example: Ius also gives jurist and jury.
items.exampleCN: ius 还给出 jurist 与 jury。
dicere 给出 verdict 与 predict。

items.example: The iudex spoke after both parties.
Iudicium is the base of judicial.
items.exampleCN: iudicium 是 judicial 的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns a trial into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把审判变成形容词。

items.example: Judicial notice is a narrow doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 司法认知是一项范围很窄的学说。

items.example: A judicious cut saved the budget.
items.exampleCN: 一次明智的削减救了预算。

items.example: Delay was prejudicial to the defence.
The judiciary answers to no minister.
items.exampleCN: 司法系统不对任何部长负责。

latinEntries.meaning: of a judge or a trial

definition_zh: 国民收入；一国居民与企业在一定时期内获得的收入总和，用于衡量经济规模
definition_en: the total income earned by the residents and businesses of a country over a period, used as a measure of the size and health of its economy
core_image: 一间国家账房把千万户的工资、租金与利润汇进同一本总账，账页越厚，经济规模越大
scene: 二十世纪三十年代的统计员第一次把全国工资与利润加进同一本账。 Economists use national income to compare how much a country produces and earns in a year.
sceneCN: 此处指「一国居民与企业在一定时期内获得的收入总和」（第 1 个义项：全国收入的汇总量）；句意为经济学家用国民收入比较一国一年内的产出与收入。图中可辨识物件：木制账台、成摞账簿、算盘、写满数字的黑板。

pos.zh: 国民收入（一国居民与企业在一定时期内获得的收入总额）
（经济学的）国民收入总量指标

forms.label: 复数（不同国家或不同年度的总量）

senses.title: Total income of a nation
senses.definition: the sum of all incomes earned by a country's households and firms within a given period
senses.definitionCN: 一国居民与企业在一定时期内所得收入的总和
senses.example: National income rose faster than the population, so income per head improved.
senses.exampleCN: 国民收入增长快于人口增长，因此人均收入提高了。
senses.why: The phrase joins a whole country with money coming in, so its first reading is a national total.
senses.whyCN: 这个词组把「整个国家」与「进来的钱」直接放在一起，因此第一层意思就是全国的收入总量。

senses.title: The official accounting measure
senses.titleCN: 国民经济核算的官方口径
senses.definition: the aggregate figure compiled under national accounts rules, usually net of depreciation and adjusted for earnings from abroad
senses.definitionCN: 按国民核算规则编制的总量数字，通常扣除折旧并对境外收入作出调整
senses.example: The statistics office publishes national income every quarter using the same accounting rules.
senses.exampleCN: 统计部门每季度按同一套核算规则公布国民收入。
senses.why: Once governments needed comparable numbers, a loose national total was fixed into a formal accounting measure.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要可比的数字之后，原本笼统的全国总量被固定成正式的核算口径。

senses.title: Income actually received by residents and firms
senses.titleCN: 居民与企业实际收到的收入
senses.definition: the income actually paid out to households and businesses, before or after taxes depending on the measure used
senses.definitionCN: 实际支付给家庭与企业的收入，按所用口径决定是税前还是税后
senses.example: Wages and profits both feed into national income at the point where they are paid out.
senses.exampleCN: 工资与利润在支付出去的那一刻都计入国民收入。
senses.why: The total is built from payments actually made, so it can be read as the income that people and firms receive.
senses.whyCN: 总量由实际支付构成，因此也可理解为个人与企业收到的收入。

senses.title: National measure distinct from domestic product
senses.titleCN: 与国内产出相区别的国民口径
senses.definition: a measure of income earned by a country's residents, including earnings abroad and excluding income earned locally by foreigners
senses.definitionCN: 衡量本国居民所得收入的指标，包含境外收入，但不含外国人在本地赚取的收入
senses.example: National income differs from domestic product when many citizens work abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 当大量公民在海外工作时，国民收入与国内产出就会不同。
senses.why: Domestic product counts what is produced inside the borders, while national income follows who earns it, so the two separate when money crosses borders.
senses.whyCN: 国内产出算的是境内生产了多少，国民收入看的是收入归谁，钱一跨国界两者就分开。

senses.title: A yardstick for comparing countries
senses.titleCN: 用于比较各国经济水平的指标
senses.definition: a figure used to rank or compare countries by the total income their economies generate
senses.definitionCN: 用来按经济所产生的收入总量排列或比较各国的数字
senses.example: Analysts put national income per person beside life expectancy when they rank countries.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人员排列各国时，把人均国民收入与预期寿命并列。
senses.why: A comparable total makes a convenient yardstick, so the term took on the role of a cross-country benchmark.
senses.whyCN: 可比的总量最方便当尺子，这个词因此承担起跨国比较基准的角色。

senses.title: The shares going to wages, profits and rents
senses.titleCN: 国民收入在工资、利润与租金之间的分配
senses.definition: the division of a country's total income among wages, profits, rents and other payments to the owners of production
senses.definitionCN: 把一国收入总量分给工资、利润、租金及其他生产要素报酬
senses.example: Economists asked how national income was split between workers and owners.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家追问国民收入在劳动者与所有者之间如何划分。
senses.why: A total can also be examined from the inside as slices belonging to different earners, which is the distribution sense.
senses.whyCN: 总量也可以从内部看，分成属于不同收入者的几块，这就是分配义。

senses.title: The published statistic
senses.definition: the number or set of figures reported in official statistics and news reports
senses.definitionCN: 官方统计与新闻报道中报出的数字或一组数字
senses.example: The revised national income figure was higher than the earlier estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 修正后的国民收入数字高于早先的估计。
senses.why: An abstract total becomes a concrete number once it is printed, so the phrase also names the reported statistic itself.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的总量一经公布就成了具体数字，因此这个词组也指报出的统计数字本身。

senses.title: The theoretical aggregate in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学理论中的总量概念
senses.definition: the economy-wide total of incomes used in models of demand, saving and growth
senses.definitionCN: 需求、储蓄与增长模型所使用的全国收入总量
senses.example: In the model, national income determines how much households can spend.
senses.exampleCN: 在模型中，国民收入决定家庭能支出多少。
senses.why: Theory treats the whole economy as one account, so the phrase works as a variable rather than a headline number.
senses.whyCN: 理论把整个经济当成一本账，这个词组因此是模型变量，而不只是新闻标题里的数字。

intro.en: National income is a two-layer compound: the first half comes from Latin through French, the second is native English. It became an economic term only when national accounts were built. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 国民收入是一个两层来源的复合词：前半经法语来自拉丁语，后半为英语本族词。直到国民核算体系建立，它才成为经济术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Natio meant 'birth, race, people' and came from nasci 'to be born'. The noun entered English through Old French.
items.cn: natio 意为「出生、族群、人民」，出自 nasci「出生」。该名词经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin nationalis, built from natio with an adjective suffix, entered English in the sixteenth century with the sense 'belonging to a whole people'.
items.cn: 由 natio 加形容词后缀构成的 nationalis 于十六世纪进入英语，意为「属于整个民族的」。

items.en: Income joins a prefix meaning 'in' to the verb 'to come', literally 'that which comes in', and it named money received rather than money paid out.
items.cn: 收入一词由表示「进入」的前缀加动词「来」构成，字面就是「进来的东西」，指收到的钱而非付出去的钱。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers on political arithmetic began adding up a whole country's earnings, though they did not yet use the modern term.
items.cn: 十七世纪的政治算术作者开始把一国收入加总，但尚未使用今天的术语。

items.en: The term became standard in the 1930s and 1940s, when official national accounts were built to guide policy through depression and war.
items.cn: 这一术语在二十世纪三十至四十年代定型，当时为应对萧条与战争建立了官方国民核算体系。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation): the exact first appearance of the compound is not recorded, and estimates of the earliest use differ.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：这一复合词的确切首见未被记录，对最早用例的估计也有分歧。

note.en: Group one separates the totals that learners constantly confuse; group two lists measures that answer a closely related question.
note.cn: 第一组区分几个经常混淆的总量指标；第二组列出回答相近问题的其他度量。

entries.definition: GDP counts what is produced inside a country's borders, whoever produces it; national income counts what residents earn.
entries.definitionCN: 国内生产总值算的是境内生产了多少，不论生产者是谁；国民收入算的是本国居民赚了多少。

entries.definition: GNP adds citizens' earnings abroad to domestic output; it measures output, while national income measures income.
entries.definitionCN: 国民生产总值把公民的境外收入加到国内产出上，衡量的是产出，而国民收入衡量的是收入。

entries.definition: National wealth is a stock of assets at one moment; national income is a flow over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 国民财富是某一时刻的资产存量；国民收入是一段时期内的流量。

entries.definition: Net national income subtracts depreciation from the total, giving a narrower accounting figure.
entries.definitionCN: 净国民收入从总量中扣除折旧，是口径更窄的核算数字。

entries.definition: National output looks at goods and services produced, the other side of the same national account.
entries.definitionCN: 国民产出看的是生产出的商品与服务，是同一本国民账的另一面。

entries.definition: Domestic income is earned inside the country by anyone working there, regardless of nationality.
entries.definitionCN: 国内收入是境内任何人赚到的收入，不问国籍。

entries.definition: Aggregate income is the plain sum of all incomes, a term used in models rather than in official reports.
entries.definitionCN: 总收入就是所有收入的简单加总，多用于模型而非官方报告。

entries.definition: Per capita income divides the total by the number of people, turning a national figure into an average.
entries.definitionCN: 人均收入把总量除以人口，把全国数字变成平均值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real halves of the compound, real accounting phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词两半、真实的核算说法与真实的同族词。

normal.en: A whole people plus an adjective suffix gives the national half.
normal.cn: 「整个民族」加形容词后缀，就是「国家的」这一半。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'in' plus the verb 'to come' gives income, money that comes in.
normal.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加动词「来」，构成收入，也就是进来的钱。

normal.en: The two halves answer different questions: whose country, and how much came in.
normal.cn: 两半回答不同问题：属于哪个国家，以及进来了多少。

normal.en: Fixed accounting phrases keep the technical sense: national income accounts and national income statistics.
normal.cn: 固定的核算说法保留技术义：国民收入核算、国民收入统计。

normal.en: It sits beside domestic product, which counts output rather than earnings.
normal.cn: 它与国内产出并列，后者算产出而不是收入。

abstract.en: Picture one ledger on a national desk with every wage and profit written on the same page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张国家账台上摊着一本总账，每笔工资与利润都写在同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a family budget copied a million times and then added into one column.
abstract.cn: 想象一份家庭预算被复制百万次，再加进同一列。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler long enough to measure a whole country's yearly earning.
abstract.cn: 想象一把长到足以丈量一国全年收入的尺子。

examples.en: The survey found that national income had grown while the poorest households gained little.
examples.cn: 调查发现国民收入在增长，而最贫困家庭的所得几乎没有增加。

examples.en: National income is usually reported both before and after taxes.
examples.cn: 国民收入通常同时报告税前与税后两个口径。

examples.en: Comparing national income across countries requires adjusting for price differences.
examples.cn: 跨国比较国民收入需要按物价差异作出调整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「国家」加「收入」——把一国的工资、利润与租金都放进同一本账，就是国民收入

root: 拉丁 natio「出生、族群」出自 nasci「出生」，经古法语进入英语并派生形容词；后半为英语本族复合词，由表示「进入」的前缀加动词「来」构成，字面为「进来的东西」。两部分合为国民收入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: money earned across a whole country is gathered into one account, then read as a measure, a comparison, a share and a model variable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：全国赚到的钱被收进同一本账，再被读成指标、比较基准、分配份额与模型变量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a national ledger room where every wage, rent and profit is entered on one page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间国家账房，把每笔工资、租金与利润都记在同一页上。

branches.en: THE SUM ITSELF: what households and firms actually receive is added into one figure.
branches.cn: 总量本身：家庭与企业实际收到的钱被加成同一个数字。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT AND ITS PRINTED FORM: the same total becomes a formal measure and then a reported statistic.
branches.cn: 账目与印刷形态：同一个总量先成为正式指标，再成为报出的统计数字。

branches.en: THE BORDER TEST: following who earns the money separates national income from domestic product.
branches.cn: 边界检验：追问钱归谁赚，就把国民收入与国内产出分开。

branches.en: THE YARDSTICK: a comparable total serves both as a ranking device and as a model variable.
branches.cn: 尺子：可比的总量既是排名工具，也是模型变量。

branches.en: THE INSIDE VIEW: one total can also be read as slices belonging to different earners.
branches.cn: 内部视角：同一个总量也可读成属于不同收入者的几块。

intro.en: The compound is built from a Latin noun and a native English verb, and its parts also build a large family of everyday words.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由拉丁名词与英语本族动词构成，两部分还构成一大批日常词。

latinIntro.en: Natio and nasci supply the first half; the second half is native Germanic, so the compound mixes two language layers.
latinIntro.cn: 前半由 natio 与 nasci 提供；后半是日耳曼语本族词，因此这个复合词混合了两个语言层。

items.example: The nation rebuilt its ports after the war.
items.exampleCN: 战后这个国家重建了港口。

items.example: National figures hide wide differences between regions.
items.exampleCN: 全国数字掩盖了地区之间的巨大差异。

items.example: The scheme was rolled out nationally in two years.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划两年内在全国推开。

items.meaning: the state of belonging to a country
one who puts the nation first
items.example: The nationalist party gained seats in the election.
items.exampleCN: 民族主义政党在选举中赢得席位。

items.example: Household income stagnated for a decade.

items.meaning: one who comes, especially a promising newcomer
items.example: She was praised as a strong comer in the firm.
items.exampleCN: 她被称赞为公司里很有前途的新人。

derivatives.zh: 民族主义者 / 民族主义的

definition_zh: 社会化；使人学会群体规范与角色的过程；交往活动；公有化
definition_en: the process by which a person learns the norms, roles and behaviour expected in a group or society
core_image: 孩子在餐桌上学让菜、在学校学排队、在球场学合作，零散的训练连成一条把他带进群体的长线
scene: 这里指「社会化」。 Table manners at home and turn-taking at school are early forms of socialization.
sceneCN: 此处指「人通过家庭与学校学会群体规范与角色的过程」（第 1 个义项：学会在社会中如何行事的长期过程）；句意为家里的餐桌礼仪与学校的轮流训练都是社会化的早期形式。可辨识物件：餐桌、教室座位、球场、家长与老师。

pos.zh: 社会化（过程，常作不可数）
交往；社交活动（不可数）
公有化；集体化（经济义）

forms.label: 可数复数（具体过程或案例）
过去分词/形容词（已社会化的）

derivatives.zh: 交往；使适应社会；使公有化
已适应社会规范的；公有化的

senses.title: Learning a group's norms
senses.definition: the long process through which a child or newcomer learns what a group expects, from table manners to ways of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 儿童或新成员学习群体期待的长过程，从餐桌礼仪到说话方式
senses.example: Table manners at home and turn-taking at school are early forms of socialization.
senses.exampleCN: 家里的餐桌礼仪与学校的轮流训练都是社会化的早期形式。
senses.why: The word is social plus the noun ending -ization, which names a process; the base sense is therefore the process of becoming social.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 social 加名词词尾 -ization 构成，该词尾表示过程，因此基础义就是「变得合乎社会」的过程。

senses.title: Training inside institutions
senses.definition: the part of the process carried out by schools, armies, hospitals or workplaces with explicit rules
senses.definitionCN: 由学校、军队、医院或职场以明文规则执行的那部分过程
senses.example: Military socialization turns recruits into people who salute before they ask why.
senses.exampleCN: 军队的社会化把新兵变成先敬礼再问为什么的人。
senses.why: Institutions take over part of the family's work, so the same noun covers formal training with written rules.
senses.whyCN: 机构接替了家庭的一部分工作，因此同一个名词也涵盖带明文规定的正式训练。

senses.title: Political socialization
senses.definition: the process by which people acquire political attitudes, party loyalties and ideas about authority
senses.definitionCN: 人们获得政治态度、政党倾向与权威观念的过程
senses.example: Political socialization in the village began with the way elders talked about the council.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的政治社会化始于长辈谈论议会的方式。
senses.why: Politics is learned like any other norm, so the general process was given a field-specific label.
senses.whyCN: 政治像其他规范一样被学会，因此这个一般过程又被加上领域标签。

senses.title: Occupational socialization
senses.definition: the process of learning the values, vocabulary and habits of a profession during training and early work
senses.definitionCN: 在培训与入职初期学习某一职业的价值观、术语与习惯的过程
senses.example: Occupational socialization teaches young nurses how much silence is allowed at a bedside.
senses.exampleCN: 职业社会化教会年轻护士在病床边可以保持多少沉默。
senses.why: Every trade has its own unwritten rules, so the same process was named for the workplace.
senses.whyCN: 每个行业都有自己的不成文规则，于是同一过程又被加上职场的名目。

senses.title: Peer-group socialization
senses.definition: learning that happens among equals, such as children teaching one another playground rules
senses.definitionCN: 在同龄人之间发生的学习，如孩子互相传授操场规则
senses.example: Peer socialization taught him which jokes were safe in the schoolyard.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴社会化教会他哪些玩笑在校园里可以开。
senses.why: Adults are not the only teachers; equals also shape one another, which is why the process needed a peer variant.
senses.whyCN: 成年人并非唯一的教导者，同龄人也会互相塑造，因此这一过程又有同伴变体。

senses.title: Making something collective
senses.definition: the act of bringing property or services under shared or state control
senses.definitionCN: 把财产或服务转为共同或国家控制的行为
senses.example: The socialization of the mines followed the war, and the pits passed to public boards.
senses.exampleCN: 战后矿井被公有化，矿区转由公共机构管理。
senses.why: The same word for 'making social' was applied to ownership, so the economic sense grew directly from the base meaning.
senses.whyCN: 「使成为社会所有」的同一构词被用于所有权，因此经济义直接由基础义长出。

senses.title: Shaping behaviour through contact
senses.definition: in psychology, the shaping of behaviour by repeated interaction with other people rather than by instruction alone
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，通过与他人反复互动而非单纯教导来塑造行为
senses.example: The researchers studied socialization in toddlers by watching how they copied one another.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者通过观察幼儿如何互相模仿来研究他们的社会化。
senses.why: Contact with others, not instruction alone, is the engine here, which is why the word can name a psychological mechanism as well as a social process.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动力是与他人的接触而非单纯教导，因此这个词既能指社会过程，也能指心理机制。

senses.title: The act of mingling
senses.definition: the everyday activity of meeting people and taking part in group life
senses.definitionCN: 与人见面并参与群体生活的日常活动
senses.example: The weekly dinner is less a lesson than a chance for socialization.
senses.exampleCN: 每周的聚餐与其说是课程，不如说是交往的机会。
senses.why: The mass noun also names the activity itself, so the word can mean both the long process and tonight's gathering.
senses.whyCN: 这个不可数名词也指活动本身，因此既可指长过程，也可指今晚的聚会。

intro.en: Socialization is formed in English from social plus -ization, a noun ending that names a process. Social itself goes back to Latin socialis and socius 'ally'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: socialization 是英语用 social 加 -ization 构成的，后者是表示过程的名词词尾。social 本身可追溯到拉丁 socialis 与 socius「盟友」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socius meant 'ally, companion'. From it came socialis 'of companionship or alliance'.
items.cn: socius 意为「盟友、同伴」，由它构成 socialis「与结伴或联盟有关的」。

items.en: English social entered through Old French and named what belongs to companionship or to organized society.
items.cn: 英语 social 经古法语进入，指与结伴或与有组织社会有关的事物。

items.en: The verb ending -ize comes from Greek -izein, 'to make or to act', which English attached to nouns to form verbs such as socialize.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 来自希腊 -izein「使……或做……」，英语把它接在名词后构成 socialize 一类动词。

items.en: The noun ending -ation comes from Latin -atio, which names an action or a process, so socialize plus -ation yields the name of the process.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 来自拉丁 -atio，表示动作或过程，因此 socialize 加 -ation 就得到过程的名称。

items.en: Sociology adopted the term around the turn of the twentieth century to name how children acquire the ways of their group.
items.cn: 社会学在二十世纪之交采用这个词，用来命名儿童习得群体行事方式的过程。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of socialization in the technical sense is not precisely dated, and estimates differ, so no exact year is claimed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：socialization 在术语意义上的最早英语用例缺乏精确考证，各家估计不一，因此不给出确切年份。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same social root; group two holds processes of learning or absorbing a culture that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 social 词根的词；第二组是常与社会化混淆的学习或文化吸收过程。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to mix or to train into norms; socialization is the noun for the process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为交往或使人适应规范的动词；socialization 是表示过程的名词。

entries.definition: Means of interaction or society; it describes a quality, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为交往或社会的，描述性质而非过程。

entries.definition: Describes the level of society as a whole; it does not name a learning process.
entries.definitionCN: 描述整体社会层次，不指学习过程。

entries.definition: Describes a person already trained or a resource already made public; the noun names the training itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已受训练的人或已公有化的资源；名词则指训练本身。

entries.definition: The process of acquiring one's own culture, often used by anthropologists; socialization is the broader sociological term.
entries.definitionCN: 习得自身文化的过程，人类学者常用；socialization 是更宽的社会学术语。

entries.definition: Change that occurs when two cultures meet; it need not involve growing up in one group.
entries.definitionCN: 两种文化接触时发生的变化；不一定涉及在某一群体中成长。

entries.definition: The fuller absorption of a minority into a majority culture; socialization can occur without any such absorption.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体被主流文化较完整地吸收；社会化未必包含这种吸收。

entries.definition: The way parents raise a child; socialization also happens outside the home, in schools, media and peer groups.
entries.definitionCN: 父母养育孩子的方式；社会化还发生在家庭之外，如学校、媒体与同伴群体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Social plus -ization: the ending turns an adjective into the name of a process.
normal.cn: social 加 -ization：这个词尾把形容词变成过程的名称。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stage: early socialization, primary socialization, occupational socialization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：早期社会化、初级社会化、职业社会化。

normal.en: The family runs socialize, socialized, socializing, social and society.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 socialize、socialized、socializing、social 与 society。

normal.en: The verb ending is Greek and the noun ending is Latin, so the word is another hybrid of the learned vocabulary.
normal.cn: 动词词尾来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，因此这个词也是学术词汇中的混合体。

normal.en: The economic sense uses the same shape: the socialization of the mines means their transfer to public ownership.
normal.cn: 经济义沿用同一词形：矿井的公有化即转归公共所有。

abstract.en: Picture a child slowly learning the unspoken rules of a room without ever being told them aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从未被明说，却慢慢学会一间屋子里的不成文规则。

abstract.en: Picture a river that carries each new arrival into the same current as everyone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，把每个新来者带进与众人相同的水流。

abstract.en: Picture a private road being opened at once to every family on the hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一条私家路突然向山上每户人家开放。

examples.en: Socialization at home taught her to wait until the eldest had spoken.
examples.cn: 家庭的社会化教会她等长辈开口后再说话。

examples.en: The school's hidden curriculum is part of socialization, not part of the syllabus.
examples.cn: 学校的隐性课程属于社会化的一部分，而不在教学大纲里。

examples.en: The socialization of the railway network took a decade of legislation.
examples.cn: 铁路网的公有化花了十年立法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社会的）+ ization（过程）」——把人带进社会的过程 → 社会化

root: socialization 由 social 加 -ization 构成；social 来自拉丁 socialis，词根 socius「盟友」；-ize 来自希腊 -izein，-ation 来自拉丁 -atio。该词作为社会学概念在二十世纪之交普及，最早书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one process outward: learning norms at home, then in institutions, politics and work, then among peers, then the collective and psychological readings, and finally the everyday activity itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一过程向外展开：先在家里学规范，再在学校、政治与职场中学，随后在同伴间学，继而分出集体义与心理义，最后落到日常交往活动本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where each newcomer is quietly shown how to pass, wait and speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，每个新来者都被安静地示范怎样递菜、等待与开口。

branches.en: BASE PROCESS: the noun names the long becoming-social of a person.
branches.cn: 基础过程：这个名词指一个人逐渐变得合乎社会的长过程。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND POLITICS: schools, armies and parties take over part of the teaching.
branches.cn: 机构与政治：学校、军队与政党接替了一部分教导工作。

branches.en: OCCUPATION: a trade adds its own unwritten rules to the general ones.
branches.cn: 职业：行业在一般规则之上再加自己的不成文规则。

branches.en: PEERS AND CONTACT: equals and repeated interaction shape behaviour without formal instruction.
branches.cn: 同伴与接触：同龄人与反复互动在无正式教导的情况下塑造行为。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE AND ACTIVITY: the same word covers shared ownership and the plain act of mingling.
branches.cn: 集体与活动：同一个词既指共同所有，也指单纯的交往行为。

intro.en: The word is assembled from an English adjective and two endings of Greek and Latin origin, one for the verb and one for the noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由英语形容词加两个来源分别为希腊与拉丁的词尾装配而成，一个构成动词，一个构成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius supplies the root; Greek -izein supplies the verb ending; Latin -atio supplies the noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 提供词根；希腊 -izein 提供动词词尾；拉丁 -atio 提供名词词尾。

items.example: The verb socialize is built with this ending.
items.exampleCN: 动词 socialize 由这个词尾构成。

items.meaning: to mix or to train into norms

items.meaningCN: 已社会化的；已公有化的
items.example: The pupils were socialized into the routine.
items.exampleCN: 学生们已被训练适应这套作息。
这些影响属于社会层面。

derivatives.meaning: to mix socially or to train into norms
